findings.title: Item.QualityFromLink cannot parse the 11.1.5+ |cnIQ<n> item-link color; tests pin the retired |cff format
findings.locations: LibKa0s/Item.lua:85; LibKa0s/Item.lua:75; tests/test_item.lua:14-16; LootHistory/core/Compat.lua:163; LootHistory tests/test_itemsetup.lua:14
findings.evidence: Pattern link:match("|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)") only matches |c+8 hex; since patch 11.1.5 item links use |cnIQ<n> (warcraft.wiki.gg ItemLink / UI_escape_sequences), so every live link on 120100 returns nil. LootHistory's Compat.GetItemInfo falls back to it for uncached items, so those drops are recorded with nil quality. All three test cases and LootHistory's fixture use the pre-11.1.5 |cff shape, so they pass anyway.
findings.remediation: C-01 (Item minor 1->2): add a rung reading tonumber(link:match("|cnIQ(%d+)")) ahead of the hex rung (anchor on digits, don't require trailing ':'); keep the hex rung for stored legacy links. Add |cnIQ fixtures, keep |cff as legacy-rung case (red under: drop the |cnIQ rung). Update docs/api/Item version-2 docs + members-2.json, test-cases.md and README badge in same commit. Smoke S-001. Consumer follow-up M6-T14: refresh LootHistory tests/test_itemsetup.lua EPIC_LINK to |cnIQ shape.

verification.reason: LibKa0s/Item.lua:85 matches only "|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)", so a live 11.1.5+ '|cnIQ<n>:' link returns nil. tests/test_item.lua:14-16 uses only the legacy |cff shape. LootHistory/core/Compat.lua:163 falls back to NS.Item.QualityFromLink when C_Item.GetItemInfo returns nothing (the item is uncached). That is the common case at loot time, so drops are saved with nil quality. This is lasting data damage, which justifies high. The remediation (a digit-anchored cnIQ rung ahead of the hex rung, with the legacy rung kept) is sound and additive.

findings.title: PageBanner/PageHeader/divider leak an AceGUI Dropdown or raw Frame plus a texture on every full page render
findings.evidence: O.PageBanner does AceGUI:Create("Dropdown") each render, O.PageHeader CreateFrame each call, drawChromeDivider creates a new texture each call; releaseLedger only Hide()/SetParent(nil)s them, never AceGUI:Release. Unbounded growth per render in 8 consumers' banner/header pages (AuraMaster, ConsumableMaster, KickCD, MultiMeters, AbsorbTracker, PanelMaster). Kit mock AceGUI never reuses widgets so no test can see it. Side issue: SetParent(nil) on a texture Region unverified.
findings.remediation: C-02 (OptionsTabs minor 3->4, new Options version key): pool PageHeader frame per ctx (ctx.__headerPool via LibKa0s-Pool-1.0, released in releaseChrome via Pool.ReleaseAll); build divider texture once per ctx (ctx.__ruleTex), hide on release, never SetParent(nil) a Region; keep ctx.__bannerWidget and AceGUI:Release it at top of next releaseChrome. Kit revision +1: mock AceGUI Create/Release per-type survey in testkit/mock_record.lua with 2-line hook in mock_base.lua. New tests in tests/test_options_tabs.lua (second render releases first dropdown; header frame reused; divider drawn once per ctx). Smoke S-002.

verification.reason: The leak is real. OptionsTabs.lua:1036 calls AceGUI:Create("Dropdown") on every PageBanner render. :1117 calls CreateFrame on every PageHeader. drawChromeDivider at :577 calls edgeTexture on every call. releaseLedger at :734-741 only does Hide() and SetParent(nil), and nothing calls AceGUI:Release. testkit/mock_base.lua ~1364 documents that the fake never reuses a widget. The severity drops to medium: the growth is one frame (plus its texture or dropdown) per full page render. Only the player triggers those renders in the options window, so this is a slow leak you can reach. It is not hot-path or combat growth.

findings.title: Slash CliSet/CliReset ignore the write seam's false,err refusal and echo the unchanged value
findings.evidence: Schema.Set returns false, invalid, why on validate rejection; CliSet discards it and prints path = <old value>. CliReset likewise ignores ApplyDefault false. BankLedger passes Schema.Set directly; MultiMeters has 14 validated rows; AuraMaster hand-prints the refusal in its own wrapper.
findings.remediation: C-03 (Slash minor 14->15): capture ok, err = d.set(row.path, v); if ok == false print INVALID(path) plus indented err and return, else echo. CliReset prints new NO_DEFAULT string when applyDefault returns exactly false. Document that set may answer false, reason (nil/true unchanged). Tests in tests/test_slash.lua or new tests/test_slash_refusal.lua if over 1500 lines. Consumer follow-up M6-T13: AuraMaster wrapper becomes return NS.SetByPath(path, v) and drops its own prints; re-check other hosts' wrappers. Smoke S-003.

verification.reason: Slash.lua:688 calls `d.set(row.path, v)` and discards the return value. It then echoes read(row.path), which is the unchanged old value. Schema.lua:451 answers `false, invalid, why` when validation rejects. CliReset (~:703) likewise ignores applyDefault's return. So a user sees their /set silently fail with no reason given. The remediation is additive and keeps nil/true meaning success. tests/test_slash.lua is 1327 lines, so the split-file caveat is appropriate.

findings.title: Media.RegisterLSM registers JetBrains Mono without a langmask (refused on ruRU/CJK) but still counts it; comment wrong
findings.evidence: LSM refuses a font with no langmask on non-Western clients (LibSharedMedia-3.0.lua:247-249 returns false); call passes no mask and ignores return, so on ruRU/koKR/zhCN/zhTW the face is never registered while count reports 1. Comment claims identical triples cost nothing, but each consumer registers a different path; first registration wins.
findings.remediation: C-04 (Media minor 3->4): pass LSM.LOCALE_BIT_western + LSM.LOCALE_BIT_ruRU as langmask; count a font/statusbar only if LSM:IsValid(type, name) after registering; rewrite the comment (first registration wins; every consumer's path names identical bytes). Test with fake non-western LSM in tests/test_media.lua. Smoke S-004 (ruRU + enUS).

verification.reason: Media.lua:274-275 calls LSM:Register(font, name, path) with no langmask and counts it regardless. In LibSharedMedia-3.0.lua (vendored copy, ~line 245), Register returns false for a font whose langmask is nil when the locale is non-Western. Register also returns false when the key is already registered (first wins), so the comment at Media.lua:251-253 ('costs nothing', 'identical triple') is misleading. lib.FONTS holds only JetBrains Mono, which has Cyrillic glyphs, so the western+ruRU mask is correct and CJK is rightly excluded. Counting through IsValid is fine.

findings.title: A later-loading newer AceEvent-3.0 re-embed silently overwrites the Bus tracking wrappers
findings.evidence: AceEvent-3.0 upgrade loop re-Embeds every target, overwriting the six members including Bus wrappers; later registrations go straight to CallbackHandler and are never recorded, so StandDown leaves them live (anti-pattern #85 draw gate) or StandUp never replays them. Latent: needs a third-party addon shipping a newer AceEvent minor.
findings.remediation: C-05 (Bus minor 1->2): keep rec.wrap[kind]; add restamp(rec) that re-assigns any member not equal to its wrapper and adopts the new raw member as rec.raw[kind]; keep a weak-keyed created list beside held and restamp every created target in StandDown/StandUp, returning a trailing restamped count via isDown's debug seam. Document the residual window in the docstring. Test in tests/test_bus.lua simulating re-embed (red under: drop restamp). Smoke S-005. Do not fork Ace3 or use a metatable proxy.

verification.reason: The mechanism is real. Bus.lua:152-184 stamps wrappers onto the members of an AceEvent:Embed'd target. AceEvent-3.0's upgrade path re-embeds every target in AceEvent.embeds, which overwrites RegisterEvent and the other members with the raw versions. From then on StandDown/StandUp no longer track new registrations. But it only happens when a third-party addon ships a newer AceEvent-3.0 minor that loads after a Ka0s addon has created targets. That minor has been stable for years, and the finding itself calls it latent. There is no current path to it, so severity drops to low. The remediation is sound, including the documented window before restamp.

findings.title: Launcher click has no disabled-state seam; three hosts hand-write the rung (a)/(b) refusal differently
findings.evidence: launcher-§2 requires a disabled left-click on rung (a)/(b) to be refused with the dispatcher's line; the one OnClick owner (anti-patterns #81) has no isEnabled field, so BankLedger, AuraMaster and AbsorbTracker each gate inside onClick in three spellings; a host that forgets writes SavedVariables while disabled (#85).
findings.remediation: C-06 (Launcher minor 1->2): add optional descriptor fields isEnabled (function) and disabledLine (function returning the Slash line); in click, when left button, onClick present and not isEnabled(), emit disabledLine() and return. Rung (c) still expressed by omitting onClick. Tests for rung (a) refused, rung (c) unchanged, right-click unchanged. Consumer follow-up M6-T12: each rung (a)/(b) host passes the two fields and deletes its hand-written gate, one commit per host. Serialize after M5-T1 (shared tests/test_launcher.lua). Smoke S-006.

verification.reason: Launcher.lua:178-185 click() has no enabled gate, and the descriptor docs at :98-127 have no isEnabled field. launcher.md:32 does require a disabled rung (a)/(b) left-click to be refused. All three current rung (a)/(b) hosts do implement the refusal: BankLedger LauncherSetup:156, AuraMaster :119-120 and AbsorbTracker :160-161. So nothing is broken today. This is duplication, a design gap, with only a hypothetical future host at risk. Severity drops to low. The remediation (optional isEnabled/disabledLine, rung (c) unchanged) is sound and additive.

findings.title: 23 assertError calls only assert that something raised; four pass the expected text as the failure message
findings.locations: tests/test_launcher.lua:123-128; tests/test_kit_inventory.lua:173,182,190,202,230; tests/test_mock_ace.lua (9 calls); tests/test_loader.lua:116-117; tests/test_options_compose.lua:674-675; tests/test_schema.lua:548; testkit/framework.lua:266-273

They are in test_kit_inventory 173/182/190/202/230, test_launcher 123-128 (x4, where the expected text is passed only as the failure message), test_loader 116-117, test_mock_ace 119/120/137/402/403/488/617/618/629 (9), test_options_compose 674-675 and test_schema 548. framework.lua:266-273 uses msg only as failure text. findings.title: Core printer.Format raises on a secret value in a numeric specifier (bug DebugLog already fixed)
findings.evidence: Args are stringified first; a secret becomes "<secret>" and %d/%.1f raises 'number expected, got string' in combat. DebugLog added a pcall + verbatim fallback for the identical failure. Latent: 0 current consumer call sites pass a numeric specifier through printer.Format.
findings.remediation: C-07 (Core minor 7->8): pcall(string.format, SafeToString(fmt), unpack(parts)); on failure join fmt and parts with spaces; emit. No floor raise. Test in tests/test_core.lua (secret into %d lands as format + <secret>; red under: remove pcall). Smoke S-007.

verification.reason: The mechanism is real. In Core.lua:455-460 printer.Format stringifies every argument through SafeToString, then calls fmt:format(unpack(parts)) with no pcall. A secret becomes '<secret>', and %d on that raises. DebugLog.lua:640-658 already guards the identical failure. Ordinary numbers still format, because Lua 5.1 coerces numeric strings. The finding itself counts 0 current call sites passing a numeric specifier through printer.Format, so it is latent. Severity drops to low. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: Launcher missing-library notices repeat on every Register and are double-tagged [LibKa0s]
findings.evidence: Register is callable from OnInitialize and login, so NO_BROKER/NO_ICON/NO_MINIMAP print twice; strings start "[LibKa0s] %s:" and go through the host's tagged printer. Only reachable where broker libs are missing.
findings.remediation: Part of C-06: guard each notice with once[key] per instance; drop the "[LibKa0s] " tag from the values (keys unchanged, L overrides still work). Test one NO_ICON across two Register calls.

verification.reason: LibKa0s/Launcher.lua:198 short-circuits only when object and iconLib are both set, so every failing Register reaches emit at :203, :228 or :235 again and prints again. STRINGS at :70-75 hard-code the "[LibKa0s] %s:" prefix, and makeEmit (:79-84) hands them to d.print, the host's printer, which usually adds its own tag. The notices only fire when the broker or icon libraries are missing, so low is the right severity. One caveat for the remediation: in the DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME fallback the untagged line still carries the addon name through %s, so dropping the tag is acceptable.

findings.title: DebugLog buffer trims with O(n) table.remove(1) on every line at the cap
findings.evidence: At the 1500-line MAX_BUFFER every Add shifts 1500 slots; only under debug logging.
findings.remediation: C-11 (DebugLog minor 12->13): ring buffer with head index; BufferSize/LastLine/FindLine/CopyText walk in order. D.buffer is public: grep consumers for .buffer; keep an ordered lazily-rebuilt view or fall back to batched trim (compact every 64). Characterization cases first (testing-§13), plus '1501st line drops the first'. Smoke S-008.

verification.reason: LibKa0s/DebugLog.lua:623 runs table.remove(D.buffer, 1) once the buffer holds more than MAX_BUFFER (1500, :57) lines, so every Add at the cap costs O(n). It only happens with debug logging on, and a memmove of 1500 slots is cheap, so low (arguably info). D.buffer is a public contract: tests/test_debuglog.lua:87-142 index it directly, and :117-119 already covers eviction of the oldest lines. A ring buffer would break those tests, so the batched trim (or a kept ordered view) is the safer option the remediation already names.

findings.title: Perf gate comment says 'no metatable' but instance has one; nil-initialized fields hit __index/__newindex every sampler frame
findings.evidence: P.armed/P.recording/P.label are assigned nil so never raw keys; every onUpdate read calls the __index closure. P.on gate is raw so performance-§2 holds; cost small, only during perf runs.
findings.remediation: C-12 (Perf minor 12->13): rawset(P, k, false) for armed/recording/label before setmetatable (audit == nil reads first); rewrite comment (gate is a raw field; metatable only for suspended). Keep tests/test_perf_isolation.lua 0 KB pin green.

verification.reason: The finding is real. Perf.lua:400-405 assigns P.armed and P.recording nil, so neither is a raw key, and :940-941 reads P.recording and P.armed on every sampler frame through the __index closure (:424-428). The P.on gate stays raw, so performance-§2 holds. The comment at :400-401 ('no metatable') is stale. The remediation is incomplete, though: rawset(P,k,false) before setmetatable only helps until the next nil write, because assigning nil to a raw key removes it and the reads fall back to __index. openWindow :911 (P.armed=nil), closeWindow :921 (P.recording=nil), :959, :1011, :1033 and :1044 (P.label=nil) all write nil. Every one of them has to write false. Readers tolerate false: :307-308 compares strings, P.LABELS[false] answers nil, and 'if not w' is fine.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-12 (Perf minor 12->13): initialize armed/recording/label as false (plain assignment works before setmetatable). Change every later nil write to false (Perf.lua:911, :921, :959, :1011, :1033, :1044) so the keys stay raw, and audit any '== nil' reads of these fields first. Rewrite the :400-401 comment: P.on is a raw field and the metatable exists only for 'suspended'. Keep the tests/test_perf_isolation.lua 0 KB pin green, and add a case asserting rawget(P,'recording') ~= nil after a window closes.

findings.title: ReorderList hijacks the host row frame's OnUpdate and caches its drop line on the AceGUI-pooled container
findings.evidence: Drag poll SetScript("OnUpdate") on row.frame then clears it, overwriting any host OnUpdate; container.__ka0sDropLine rides back into AceGUI's pool keeping the first caller's lineColor, contradicting the file's own pooled-frame rule. No shipped row frame carries an OnUpdate today.
findings.remediation: C-10 (Widgets minor 9->10): run the poll on the library-owned ghost frame (ghost.__row), clear the ghost's script in finishDrag/Cancel; drop line from a per-process pool, re-parented per Finish with current list's color, reclaimed in Cancel. Tests in new tests/test_widgets_reorder.lua (test_widgets.lua at 1493). Smoke S-008.

verification.reason: The defect is real. Widgets.lua:999 runs row.frame:SetScript('OnUpdate', ...) on the host's frame, and :915 and :1080 clear it with nil, which would wipe any OnUpdate the host had set. :739/:753 cache the drop line as container.__ka0sDropLine on an AceGUI-pooled container, and the colour is fixed at first creation (:748). That contradicts the file's own handle-pool rule at :783-795. No shipped row frame carries an OnUpdate today, so low is right. The rule_ref is a poor fit: events-frames-taint-§6 covers Lua over XML and object pooling for high-churn UI, not keeping library state off host-pooled frames. The violation is of the module's own documented pooled-frame invariant.
verification.corrected_remediation: Same remediation as stated (poll on the library-owned ghost frame, drop line from a library pool reclaimed in Cancel, re-coloured per list, tests in a new tests/test_widgets_reorder.lua). Change rule_ref to the Widgets.lua:783-795 pooled-frame invariant (internal) instead of events-frames-taint-§6.

findings.title: Item quality-color map cached even when built empty; LoadItem waits a fixed 0.4s timer
findings.evidence: If first call precedes ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS population the empty map persists for the session; LoadItem fires after C_Timer.After(0.4) regardless of data arrival. Unlikely in client; less relevant once |cnIQ rung lands.
findings.remediation: Part of C-01: build into a local and assign qualityByHex only if at least one entry landed; add empty-map retry case. Leave LoadItem unchanged (byte-identical in both hosts) and record that decision.

verification.reason: LibKa0s/Item.lua:63-71: buildQualityByHex assigns qualityByHex = {} before it checks ITEM_QUALITY_COLORS, and :87 only rebuilds when the map is nil, so an empty map built early is kept for the whole session. The comment at :57-60 names exactly this failure mode, but the code only half-avoids it. LoadItem at :124 fires cb after a fixed C_Timer.After(0.4) whether or not the data arrived. It is unlikely in the client, so low. The remediation (commit only a non-empty map, leave LoadItem alone and record why) is sound.

findings.title: A Perf bracket left open by an error misattributes later brackets' observed parent for the rest of the run
findings.evidence: openDepth only reset in P.Reset (from Start); a host raise between Open and Close leaves the slot open so later Close records the leaked key as observedWithin; window open/close doesn't reset.
findings.remediation: Part of C-12: reset openDepth = 0 in openWindow and closeWindow. Test in tests/test_perf_core.lua: leaked Open in window A does not parent a bracket in window B.

verification.reason: Perf.lua:550 increments openDepth on Open, and Close (:569-584) only lowers it for a matched key. If a host error lands between Open and Close, the slot stays open below later brackets. The only reset is P.Reset at :592, not openWindow (:909) or closeWindow (:919), so a later nested Close reports the leaked key as its parent (:581), even in a different window. findings.title: Lifecycle edge is re-entrant and the file doesn't document it
findings.evidence: A standDown callback that takes/releases a hold fires a nested edge (standUp inside unwinding standDown); latch stays consistent but host teardown can interleave. No shipped callback touches the latch.
findings.remediation: C-13 (Lifecycle minor 1->2): document in New's docstring that a callback MUST NOT take or release a hold (or queue nested edges), and add a tests/test_lifecycle.lua case pinning the chosen nested-edge behavior.

verification.reason: LibKa0s/Lifecycle.lua:123-129 edge() sets `down` then calls d.standDown()/d.standUp() synchronously; a Release inside standDown would re-enter edge() and fire standUp nested. New's docstring (:75-89) says nothing about re-entrancy, and grep for reentr/nested finds nothing in Lifecycle.lua, tests/test_lifecycle.lua or docs/api/Lifecycle. No shipped callback does this, so low is right. A comment change still changes the file's bytes, so the Lifecycle minor bump and a docs/api/Lifecycle update are right. This is LibKa0s's own payload, so the non-upstream routing is correct.

findings.locations: docs/releasing.md:157; docs/automated-tests/*/manifest.json; tags v1.28.0, v1.29.0, v1.36.0, v1.36.1, v1.54.1, v1.54.2

Since 2026-09-08, exactly v1.28.0, v1.29.0, v1.36.0, v1.36.1, v1.54.1 and v1.54.2 have no bundle naming them, and v1.54.1/v1.54.2 were tagged 5 minutes apart. docs/releasing.md step 7 says 'No tag is cut without a bundle whose release field names it'. findings.title: Payload registers client events raw on private frames with no pcall'd per-event isolation or rejected-name record
findings.evidence: f:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED"/"PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED") on combat-lock frame and m:RegisterEvent("GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN") on popup menu; events-frames-taint-§1 (binds per library-stack-§7) requires a single pcall'd helper, player-reachable rejected-name record, AceEvent over private frames. Not reachable today; no register row records why. Note: the library cannot floor on consumer-vendored AceEvent (library-stack-§6), a tension the audit resolves locally via a register row rather than flagging against the standard.
findings.remediation: Owner decision. (a) Code: module-local safeRegister(frame, event) that pcalls RegisterEvent, records rejected names in lib.__rejectedEvents surfaced via DebugLog/Core printer; use at the three sites; minors for OptionsTabs/Widgets (+ helper owner), API docs, tests, re-vendor (must not raise or print per event per frame). (b) Recommended: register row events-frames-taint-§1 in CLAUDE.md (library can't floor on AceEvent; widget-owned frames; stable core events), re-check trigger: a post-current-expansion event or a fourth registration site. If (a), batch with the review's OptionsTabs/Widgets minors (C-02, C-10).

verification.reason: The cited call sites are real: OptionsTabs.lua:102-103 and :139-140 (PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/ENABLED on lib.__combatFrame) and Widgets.lua:393 (GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN on the popup menu). No CLAUDE.md register row mentions events-frames-taint. Two parts of the evidence are wrong, though. (1) library-stack-§7's 'every rule above applies' refers to library-stack's own earlier rules (§1-§6). It does not import events-frames-taint-§1, and §1's text is addressed to an addon (`addon:RegisterEvent`, a module's disable path, the player-facing debug verb). The binding is therefore interpretive, not the stated rule. (2) The claim that the library 'cannot floor on consumer-vendored AceEvent' is contradicted by the library itself: library-stack-§7's Bus row says Bus.lua resolves AceEvent-3.0 at call time. The reachable impact is nil. All three names are stable core client events, and the per-event-isolation clause exists to stop one retired name from deafening a block, which cannot happen with PLAYER_REGEN_*/GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN. These are widget-owned UI frames, not addon event traffic. Info fits better than low. Option (b), a register row, is the right disposition. Option (a) adds a helper, minors and a re-vendor for no reachable benefit.
verification.corrected_remediation: Record a CLAUDE.md register row for events-frames-taint-§1. It covers the widget-owned private frames in OptionsTabs.lua (combat lock, PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/ENABLED) and Widgets.lua (popup-menu dismiss, GLOBAL_MOUSE_DOWN). Reasons: the section is written against addon event traffic; these frames carry UI state for one widget; and the three names are stable core events, so one-bad-name isolation cannot trigger. Do not justify the row with 'the library cannot use AceEvent', because Bus.lua already resolves AceEvent at call time. Re-check trigger: registering any event newer than the current expansion, or a fourth private registration site. Make no code change unless the owner chooses the pcall'd-helper route. If they do, batch it with the OptionsTabs/Widgets minors already planned.

findings.title: /at profile new <existing name> silently switches to and resets that profile, then prints 'Created ... new profile'
findings.evidence: new = needsName(... db:SetProfile(name); NS.ResetProfileCounted(db); print("Created and switched to new profile '"..name.."'")). When the name already exists, SetProfile switches to it and ResetProfile empties it, with no confirmation. The help text and docs promise 'Create new profile with defaults'. Tests cover only a fresh name.
findings.remediation: C-01: add a profileExists(db,name) helper that walks db:GetProfiles(). new refuses an existing name with one line pointing to /at profile use <name> and /at profile reset. Update the comment at :427-430, docs/profiles.md:79 and docs/smoke-tests.md. Red-first test: seed units.player.barWidth=333 on Keep, run 'new Keep', assert Keep still holds 333 and the current profile has not changed (-- red under: removing the profileExists guard).

verification.reason: settings/Slash.lua:431-435 runs db:SetProfile(name) then NS.ResetProfileCounted(db) with no existence check. The comment at :427-430 even says 'new on a name that already exists resets that profile'. PROFILE_HELP at :383 promises 'Create new profile with defaults'. The only test (tests/test_slashcmds.lua:544) uses a fresh name 'Fresh'. So typing '/at profile new Default' irreversibly wipes the live profile and prints a false 'Created' line. That is silent data loss from one typed command, so High stands. The remediation (a profileExists guard with a red-first test) is sound.

findings.title: /at profile copy raises a real AceDB Lua error on a missing or current name; /at profile delete <missing> reports a deletion that did not happen
findings.evidence: copy calls db:CopyProfile(name) bare, and AceDB errors on a missing source or on self-copy. delete calls db:DeleteProfile(name,true), which is a no-op for a missing name, and then prints 'Deleted profile'. A scratch probe printed '[AT] Copied settings from profile 'NoSuchProfile'' and '[AT] Deleted profile 'NoSuchProfile''. The suite passes only because the kit's AceDB fake never raises (F-006).
findings.remediation: C-02: before calling AceDB, check the name against GetCurrentProfile() and against profileExists(). Print 'Cannot copy a profile onto itself', 'Cannot delete the current profile', or 'Profile '<name>' not found — /at profile list shows them'. Do not use pcall. Add three red-first tests (copy missing, copy current, delete missing) with output assertions. They will also cover the raise once F-006 lands upstream.

verification.reason: settings/Slash.lua:437-448: copy calls db:CopyProfile(name) bare. Real AceDB (libs/AceDB-3.0/AceDB-3.0.lua:581-587) errors on a self-copy or a missing source when not silent, which gives a real Lua error in-game. delete passes silent=true, and AceDB :531-537 then no-ops for a missing name, yet the code still prints 'Deleted profile'. findings.evidence: Fresh lizard: SyncUserCategories NLOC 64, CCN 25, four sequential phases (teardown, insert points, materialize, register); renderCategories CCN 16, a three-way branch on grid kind. The newest run, 20260916-184324, is 129 commits behind: recorded 21,163 NLOC / 2,446 functions / 943 tests / 0 over CCN 15 / 0 files over cap / 2 in band; now 30,336 / 3,348 / 1,296 / 2 / 4 / 4. findings.remediation: Pin characterization tests first (testing-§13). Coverage exists in test_defaults, test_database and test_pages_filters; confirm each phase is pinned. Split SyncUserCategories into four named file-local phase helpers (teardownUserDefinitions/insertBeforePaths or insertionAnchors/materializeRecords/registerUserRows, each CCN <= 8, orchestrator <= 5; performance-§11 shapes 2/4, not a part2). For renderCategories, the review extracts renderCustomGrid; the audit prefers a module-level GRID_RENDER per-grid table (shape 1). Either works; pick one. Keep the WHY comments with the code and change no behavior. Check: fresh lizard shows 0 warnings. Regenerate the automated-tests bundle and RESULTS.md at release through the four-suite runner (bump-version), with a Disposition for every new watch-list entry.

verification.reason: A fresh bounded lizard run gives defaults/Categories.lua:1112 Cat.SyncUserCategories at NLOC 64 / CCN 25 and settings/Filters.lua:500 renderCategories at CCN 16, the only two warnings. docs/automated-tests/ holds only 20260916-184324. RESULTS.md:80 still says tests/test_database.lua has 1037 lines; wc gives 1702. findings.title: A reused container id builds a second AuraMasterAnchor<id> frame set and leaks the old one when destroyed out of combat
findings.evidence: Only instances parked under CM.MustDefer() are revived. Out of combat, CM.Sync calls inst:Destroy() and drops the instance, and the next build calls NS.Container.New(id), which creates a new anchor/engine/blocker/outline/handle/preview pool and overwrites _G.AuraMasterAnchor<id>. Ids come back on a profile switch between profiles with different container counts, on reset (ResetProfile rewinds nextContainerId) and on copy. tests/test_containermanager.lua:488/:510 cover only the deferred half.
findings.remediation: C-01: keep destroyed instances in a dormant[id] table (CM.Sync non-deferred branch: Destroy then dormant[id]=inst; destroyParked moves to dormant). In follow(), add a dormant branch that sets staleData=true and calls revive(id, d, hold); CM.Announce already queues the apply. Add Container:Revive() only if re-Show is needed. Correct the :51-63 comment. New test: A(1-5) -> B(1-2) -> A, where spyCreate 'AuraMasterAnchor3' counts 0 on return and the container draws A's data (red under: dropping the destroyed instance). Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge. In-client smoke: same table address after the round trip, and no memory climb.

verification.reason: In modules/ContainerManager.lua:107-108, CM.Sync's non-deferred branch calls inst:Destroy() and drops the instance. Destroy (modules/Container.lua:539-546) only hides frames and clears their points. The next follow() for that id (:85-93) finds no instance and no retiring entry, so it calls NS.Container.New(id). That runs CreateFrame('Frame','AuraMasterAnchor'..id, ...) again (Container.lua:43), leaking the old frame set and overwriting the global. Ids come back on a profile switch, copy or reset, which the comment at :51-63 itself acknowledges. The only reuse path is the deferred retiring table. Medium fits a real leak gated behind an uncommon action. The dormant-table remediation fits the existing revive/staleData design.

findings.title: UNIT_AURA registered via AceEvent for every unit while a 'without a duration' container exists; the standard's carve-out permits a player/pet unit-filtered frame
findings.evidence: events:RegisterEvent('UNIT_AURA', onUnitAura), where onUnitAura discards everything except player and pet. The header rationale ('vendored AceEvent has no RegisterUnitEvent') is stale: events-frames-taint-§1 now has a named carve-out that cites this addon. Offline, unitAuraOther costs 0.00013 ms/iter and 0 B. The client dispatch cost is unverified with no in-client capture. It is reachable only when a container sets durationMode to 'only without a duration'; no starter does. The audit ('checked and not filed') treats the AceEvent path as compliant and the carve-out as optional.
findings.remediation: C-02: add one private frame held on the module, TS.unitFrame = TS.unitFrame or CreateFrame('Frame'), whose OnEvent dispatches to onUnitAura. syncAuraListen opens it with RegisterUnitEvent('UNIT_AURA','player','pet') and closes it with UnregisterEvent. TS.Stop unregisters by hand. The frame is reused across disable/enable. Rewrite the :13-21 header to cite the carve-out. Tests: the test_disabled census includes the frame, and test_timedspells asserts RegisterUnitEvent with exactly player,pet. If the kit mock does not record RegisterUnitEvent, that is an upstream testkit gap, not a local mock edit. Replace the perf.lua unitAuraOther scenario with an assertion that no shared-target UNIT_AURA registration exists, and update docs/performance.md. Pre/post in-client perf captures go in docs/perf-analysis/.

verification.reason: The code matches the evidence. modules/TimedSpells.lua:121 registers UNIT_AURA through AceEvent, and onUnitAura (:111-113) keeps only player and pet. The events-frames-taint.md §1 carve-out does exist and cites this exact shape, but it is a MAY. The first bullet's MUST (use AceEvent) is what the addon does today, so this is an optional optimization, not a deviation. The header at :13-14 is only half stale. 'The vendored AceEvent has no RegisterUnitEvent' is still true, as the standard itself says. What is stale is 'never a private frame (events-frames-taint-§1)', which implies the frame is forbidden. The impact is unmeasured in the client, 0.00013 ms/iter offline, and reachable only when a container uses the non-starter 'only without a duration' mode, and registration is already gated out of combat and secrecy. That is Low, not Medium. The remediation matches the carve-out's MUSTs (held on the module, unregistered by hand in Stop, reused across cycles). The kit mock already records RegisterUnitEvent (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:226), so the 'testkit gap' contingency does not apply.
verification.corrected_remediation: Optional adoption of the events-frames-taint-§1 MAY carve-out. Hold one private frame on the module, TS.unitFrame = TS.unitFrame or CreateFrame('Frame'). Its single OnEvent dispatches to onUnitAura. syncAuraListen opens it with RegisterUnitEvent('UNIT_AURA','player','pet') and closes it with UnregisterEvent('UNIT_AURA'). TS.Stop must unregister it by hand, because AceEvent's UnregisterAllEvents does not reach it. Reuse the frame across disable/enable. Rewrite the :13-21 header: AceEvent still lacks RegisterUnitEvent, and this is the carve-out. Tests: the test_disabled census includes the frame, and test_timedspells asserts the frame's __unitEvents.UNIT_AURA == {'player','pet'} (the kit mock already records it at tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:226, so no mock work is needed). Replace the perf.lua unitAuraOther scenario, update docs/performance.md, and put pre/post in-client captures in docs/perf-analysis/ if the change is taken.

findings.title: The host re-implements LibKa0s's tabbed-page render and page-banner chrome (Helpers.RenderTabbedPage, buildContainerHeader)
findings.locations: settings/OptionsSetup.lua:659 (RenderTabbedPage), :560 collectTabs, :583 settleActiveTab, :624 renderActiveTab, :480-504 buildContainerHeader (:484 raw Dropdown, :497 raw Button); libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:3861 O.RenderTabbedSchema; libs/LibKa0s/OptionsTabs.lua:1029 O.PageBanner

The library version lacks bespoke (non-row) tabs, a per-container disabled notice, a chrome hook, and a picker+create one-row band (options-ui-§14). findings.remediation: U-1 in LibKa0s: additive fields on O.RenderTabbedSchema (tabs rendered by a host callback and placed before a group; disabledFor(cfg) + disabledNotice; chrome(ctx) hook), and an optional right-half action button on O.PageBanner. Bump the OptionsWidgets and OptionsTabs minors by 1. Existing callers are unchanged. Evaluate it against anti-pattern #55 with the other candidate consumers first. U-2: re-vendor the WHOLE LibKa0s folder into every consumer as its own commit (diff -rq empty), with a revendor bundle. Then C-04b: replace RenderTabbedPage/buildContainerHeader with RenderTabbedSchema(..., {tabs, disabledFor, disabledNotice, chrome}) and PageBanner+action, re-pointing the test_optionssetup and test_pages_* tab cases. Never patch libs/ locally. If U-1 is declined, C-04a: add a documented deviation row in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with a re-check trigger.

verification.reason: The cited evidence is accurate. settings/OptionsSetup.lua:659 defines Helpers.RenderTabbedPage with its own chrome hook and disabledNotice, and buildContainerHeader at :480-504 builds a raw AceGUI Dropdown and Button. The library ships O.RenderTabbedSchema (libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:3861, signature ctx, pageKey, afterGroup, pairWith, with no tabs/disabled/chrome fields) and O.PageBanner (OptionsTabs.lua:1029). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:821-829 has no deviation row for it. The routing is right: extend upstream additively, then re-vendor the whole folder, and never edit libs/ locally. The severity is inflated. findings.title: Event registration is bare sequential RegisterEvent calls, with no per-event pcall isolation and no record of rejected names
findings.evidence: RegisterLifecycleEvents makes eight bare self:RegisterEvent calls, ending with ADDON_RESTRICTION_STATE_CHANGED. TS.Sync registers three more, and syncAuraListen registers UNIT_AURA. An unknown name raises and takes the rest of the block with it. Every name is valid on 12.1, so this is latent.
findings.remediation: Upstream first: nominate a SafeRegisterEvent(target, event, handler, record) helper to LibKa0s-Core-1.0 (a C_EventUtils.IsEventValid front-gate plus pcall, appending refused names to a caller-owned list). Optionally, LibKa0s-DebugLog renders the rejected list inside [Init]. It clears library-stack-§7's promotion bars because every addon is bound by events-frames-taint-§1. If it ships, re-vendor the whole folder with a bundle. If declined, add a host NS.RegisterEventSafe in core/CoreSetup.lua. Route RegisterLifecycleEvents (as a loop over a module-level list), TS.Sync, syncAuraListen and the LifecycleSetup PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED hold through it. Record rejects in NS.RejectedEvents and surface them in the [Init] summary (optionally /am debug events). Test with kit M.__badEvents = {ADDON_RESTRICTION_STATE_CHANGED=true}: the other seven still register and the name is recorded (red under: bare RegisterEvent).
findings.rule_ref: events-frames-taint-§1 (an unknown event name raises; IsEventValid front-gate SHOULD)

verification.reason: core/AuraMaster.lua:57-67 has eight bare self:RegisterEvent calls. modules/TimedSpells.lua:140-142 and :121 are bare too, and so is core/LifecycleSetup.lua:71 (addon:RegisterEvent(PENDING_EVENT, ...)). events-frames-taint.md §1 says that 'A registration block MUST survive one bad name ... every RegisterEvent goes through a single pcalled helper' and that rejected names MUST be recorded and reachable by the player. grep finds no IsEventValid, pcall or safe-register helper in core/, modules/, settings/ or the vendored libs/LibKa0s, nor in the LibKa0s repo. All the names are valid on the live client, so this is latent and Low is right, though it is a MUST failure. Upstream-first with a host fallback is the right routing, and the kit's M.__badEvents exists (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725) for the test.

findings.title: Degradation stubs copy library behavior; the Options stub composers rebuild composed blocks instead of answering an empty row list
findings.locations: settings/OptionsSetup.lua:175-280 (composeBlock, ColorPair, FontGroup, BorderGroup, BarGroup, MasterControls); tests/test_optionssetup.lua:369; settings/Slash.lua:388-391 (stub.DisabledLine); core/PoolSetup.lua:17-49; docs/settings-panel.md

findings.title: CM.Init and CM.Announce build container frames while the addon is stood down, contradicting the doc comment
findings.evidence: CM.Init runs whatever the latch says. A player who logs in disabled, or switches profile while disabled, gets an anchor and a drag handle per container, left in CreateFrame's default shown state. They are empty and invisible. The comment says Init is called 'only when the addon is actually running'. The disabled suite covers only enabled->disabled.
findings.remediation: C-06: when NS.IsStoodDown(), CM.Init returns after EnsureAuraContainer + TimedSpells.Sync, and CM.Announce skips CM.Sync. LifecycleSetup standUp calls NS.ContainerManager.Sync() before ApplyVisibility. Fix the :568-569 doc. Test: log in disabled, spyCreate 'AuraMasterAnchor' counts 0; on enable the instances exist and draw (red under: CM.Init building before the latch check).

verification.reason: core/AuraMaster.lua:51 calls CM.Init outside the `if not NS.IsStoodDown()` block. modules/ContainerManager.lua:570-579 gates only StartListening; CM.Sync (:92) still runs follow() -> NS.Container.New, which does CreateFrame('Frame','AuraMasterAnchor'..id) and builds a handle (modules/Container.lua:43-51). The doc at :568-569 says Init runs 'only when the addon is actually running', which is false. CM.Announce (:127-131) also syncs while down; rebuildProfile's comment (core/AuraMaster.lua:163-165) wrongly says CM.Init reads the latch. slash-commands-§7 says only the setup list 'comes up on load in either state', so feature frames built at a disabled login go against the spirit of the rule. Nothing draws, so low is right. The remediation is sound: standUp has to call Sync before ApplyVisibility, which it does not do today (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:108-120).

findings.title: Degraded Lifecycle stub is level-triggered (runs full standUp on every SyncEnabled), where the library is edge-triggered
findings.evidence: NS.SyncEnabled calls standDown or standUp on every call, including OnInitialize before PLAYER_LOGIN and every profile switch. standUp re-registers events, arms an apply timer and re-reparents the Blizzard frames, which means redundant apply passes. It affects only installs where libs/LibKa0s failed LibStub's floor.
findings.remediation: C-07: keep a local down boolean. SyncEnabled computes want = not enabledStored() and calls standDown/standUp only when want ~= down. Test in the degraded suite (tests/degraded_env.lua): two unchanged SyncEnabled calls arm one timer, not two.
findings.rule_ref: library-stack-§7 (the stub mirrors the member's contract)

verification.reason: Real. core/LifecycleSetup.lua:128-130 calls standDown or standUp on every SyncEnabled. SyncEnabled runs from OnInitialize (core/AuraMaster.lua:32), from every profile callback (:160) and from the enabled row's onChange. standUp re-registers events and arms RequestApply. The path is reachable only when LibKa0s-Lifecycle is absent, so low. Two fixes. tests/degraded_env.lua is an environment builder, not a suite ('Not a suite (tests/run.lua does not list it)'), so the test belongs in a suite that loads it, such as tests/test_lifecycle.lua. And library-stack-§7 (:110) only says a setup file degrades to a stub. It does not say the stub must mirror the member's edge semantics, so the rule_ref is loose and this is a correctness defect, not a standards deviation. Start the local `down` at false, the library's empty-latch state, so the first SyncEnabled of an enabled load stays a no-op as it does with the library.
verification.corrected_remediation: Keep a local `down = false` in the degraded branch. SyncEnabled computes want = not enabledStored() and calls standDown/standUp only when want ~= down, then sets down = want. Add the case to tests/test_lifecycle.lua (or whichever suite already loads tests/degraded_env.lua): two unchanged SyncEnabled calls arm one apply timer and register the lifecycle events once. Classify it as correctness (degraded-path parity), not a library-stack-§7 deviation.

findings.title: The panel's Test mode checkbox is accepted while the addon is disabled, while /am test and the launcher refuse
findings.evidence: The row is bound straight to NS.Preview.SetTestMode. Ticking it while disabled silently sets NS.State.testMode = true, and the addon comes back up in test mode when enabled. The state is session-only, with no SavedVariables write.
findings.remediation: C-09: row.set refuses turning it on while NS.IsDisabled() and prints NS.Slash.DisabledLine() (one refusal line from the dispatcher). Turning it off stays allowed. Test in test_disabled.lua: a panel set while disabled leaves testMode false and prints one refusal line.

verification.reason: settings/General.lua:107-113 binds row.set straight to NS.Preview.SetTestMode(v) with no disabled gate. modules/Preview.lua:28-40 refuses only in combat, so ticking the box while disabled sets NS.State.testMode = true and sends VISIBILITY_CHANGED. The library composer adds no gate either (libs/LibKa0s/OptionsCompose.lua:526-535: 'The host binds get/set'), so the fix is correctly routed to the host. The launcher refuses while disabled (core/LauncherSetup.lua:118-122), and `test` is not in liveVerbs (settings/Slash.lua:124-133), so the dispatcher refuses it. The panel row is the one inconsistent surface. It is session-only and nothing draws while stood down, so low. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: tests/page_helpers.lua has a stray bare CR at :80, so git classifies it binary and it escapes normalization
findings.evidence: Line 80 ends \r\r\n. git ls-files --eol shows i/-text, and the blob is stored CRLF (272 CR). The E-8 working-tree one-liner counts 1 file. The kit's test_eol is green over it (the known lone-CR limit).
findings.remediation: Delete the stray \r, run git add --renormalize tests/page_helpers.lua, and confirm i/lf w/crlf. The (e) one-liner should print 0. Upstream testkit hardening is tracked separately in AuraMaster-A-18.

verification.reason: `git ls-files --eol tests/page_helpers.lua` gives `i/-text w/-text attr/text=auto eol=crlf`. Line 80 ends `\r\r\n` (checked with od). The index blob holds 272 CRs over 271 lines, and the working tree has 271 CR. The first of the two CRs on line 80 is a lone CR, and git's text=auto check treats a lone CR as binary, which is why this file escaped normalization. tests/_kit/test_eol.lua:175-185 counts only LFs that follow a CR, so it stays green over this file. line-endings.md:505-510 names the lone CR as the one-liner's known limit and still says 'No file in the collection has one'. The line-endings §7 text 'clear a red by re-checkout, never renormalize' is not violated: that text assumes the index is already correct, and here the index itself is wrong. So `--renormalize` on this one path (it skips git's CRLF-already-in-index guard) is the right fix.

findings.title: Stand-down leaves the capture context armed (openContext, lastSnapshot, _settleSince, sessionActive), so re-enabling records movements made while disabled
findings.evidence: NS.StandDown never clears these fields. A headless repro shows a deposit made while disabled written as 1 ledger row after re-enable at the same bank visit. Disabling at a bank, closing it and re-enabling elsewhere leaves openContext=BANK_FRAME, so every BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED or PLAYER_MONEY, in combat too, schedules a full rescan. That undercuts the performance-§12 exemption premise. sessionActive stays true, so later rows append to the old visit. None of the 11 test_disabled cases opens a storage context.
findings.remediation: C-01: add L:DropContext() in modules/Ledger.lua. It cancels the pending reconcile, nils openContext, lastSnapshot and _settleSince, and fires SessionChanged(false) if a context was open. Call it as step 3b inside NS.StandDown, before the bus targets are dropped. There is no second teardown path and no CloseContext flush. Add 2 test_disabled cases with red-under comments (1017 to 1019), regenerate docs/test-cases.md, move the badge, and update the ARCHITECTURE stand-down section. Smoke test C-01, cases A and B.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (What MUST stand down); performance-§6; performance-§12; testing-§12

verification.reason: The defect is real. NS.StandDown (core/BankLedger.lua:146-191) cancels timers, unregisters events, refreshes upvalues, drops the bus targets and hides windows, but it never touches NS.State.openContext, lastSnapshot, L._settleSince or State.sessionActive. The only paths that clear them are L:CloseContext (modules/Ledger.lua:803-815) and disarmGuildBankIfGone (:624-631), and both need events that are unregistered while disabled. L:Enable (:856-890) re-registers the CHANGE_EVENTS, and L:ScheduleReconcile (:670) only checks that openContext is set. So after a re-enable, the next BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED or PLAYER_MONEY diffs against the pre-disable baseline, or triggers full rescans away from the bank. The remediation is sound: DropContext before step 4 still reaches SessionWindow's __ev with SessionChanged(false), and skipping the flush is correct. Severity drops from high to medium. The trigger is narrow, because the player must disable while a bank frame is open. Away from the bank, a stale BANK_FRAME context mostly sees one-sided changes that settleBaseline re-anchors, not phantom rows. The real impact is movements from the disabled period being captured, needless rescans until the next bank open (which breaks the performance.md premise), and a session that never ends. None of that is data loss.

findings.title: 'Reset all settings' while disabled restores settings.enabled=true in the store but never re-runs the latch
findings.evidence: ResetEverything wipes db.global in place and merges defaults, bypassing the row onChange and NS.ReevaluateEnabled. Repro: stored enabled = true, IsDisabled = true, IsStoodDown = true. The checkbox says enabled while nothing records until /reload or a toggle. None of the 8 ResetEverything cases runs while disabled.
findings.remediation: C-02: after the SETTINGS_CHANGED send and before refreshAfterReset(), call NS.ReevaluateEnabled() (as OnProfileReset does). Add a test_panel case 'ResetEverything while disabled stands the addon back up' (+1). Behavior change: a reset made while disabled re-enables. Note it under API/behavior changes. Smoke test C-02. Coordinate with the BL-34 reset unification.
findings.rule_ref: options-ui-§12 (indistinguishable from a fresh install); slash-commands-§7 (re-evaluate when the stored switch can change)

verification.reason: The defect is real. Sl:ResetEverything (settings/Slash.lua:161-197) wipes db.global in place and merges defaults back, which restores settings.enabled=true (defaults/Global.lua:42). It then sends only SETTINGS_CHANGED 'reset' and calls refreshAfterReset (:119-131). Nothing calls NS.ReevaluateEnabled or NS.SetDisabledHold. The only callers are core/Database.lua:19 (profile callbacks, which never fire because there are no profiles), core/BankLedger.lua:69 (OnEnable) and the Schema row onChange (settings/Schema.lua:224), and the wipe bypasses that onChange. The panel and the reset button are setup surfaces, so they are reachable while disabled. The remediation to call NS.ReevaluateEnabled() after the reset is correct. Severity drops from high to medium. The trigger is rare (a full reset while the addon is disabled), and the effect is an addon that stays off while its checkbox says on. That means capture is silently lost until a /reload or a toggle, but no stored data is corrupted.

findings.title: Default 30-day retention silently deletes older history at login; the README never discloses it
findings.evidence: retentionDays = 30 by default. The prune runs once per session at login. The 164-line README and its FAQ never mention retention. The only disclosure is a dropdown tooltip on Settings > History.
findings.remediation: C-03: add a README FAQ row ('Does it keep my history forever? Not by default: movements older than 30 days are removed at login. Change it in Settings > History > Keep history for...'), optionally with a sentence near /bl purge. Owner decision (CP2): change the default to 0 ('Always') in defaults/Global.lua:47 and settings/Schema.lua:118. That needs no migration, because AceDB strips default-equal values. Smoke test C-03.

verification.reason: The facts are accurate. retentionDays=30 is the default (defaults/Global.lua:47, settings/Schema.lua:118). PruneOld deletes older rows (core/Database.lua:656-675) through the once-per-session OnEnterWorld prune. README.md (164 lines) has no retention mention, and the only disclosure is the dropdown tooltip. Severity drops from medium to low. This is a deliberate default that the settings UI discloses, so the gap is in the player-facing documentation, not a code defect. The cited rule is also wrong: savedvariables-§1 is 'Structure' (the defaults table shape) and says nothing about retention. The finding rests on the README being player-facing, not on a standard MUST. The remediation also has a caveat: AceDB strips default-equal values, so a player who explicitly picked 30 while 30 was the default has nothing stored. Changing the default to 0 would silently flip that player to 'Always', so the owner decision should weigh that.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-03: add a README FAQ row saying that movements older than 30 days are removed at login by default and can be kept under Settings > History > Keep history for, optionally with a note beside /bl purge. Changing the default to 0 is an optional owner decision (CP2). If taken, note that AceDB strips default-equal values, so players who deliberately chose 30 will also move to 'Always'. Record this under the Version History behavior changes. Drop the savedvariables-§1 rule citation, because this is a documentation (player-facing README) gap.

findings.title: The retention prune's C_Timer.After(5) survives the stand-down (gated, not cancelled), and the cleanupDone latch set before the timer skips the prune for the whole session
findings.locations: core/BankLedger.lua:216-229 (latch :218, C_Timer.After :220, IsStoodDown check :221-225); core/State.lua; docs/performance.md:47
findings.evidence: C_Timer.After cannot be cancelled. A disable within 5 s of the first loading screen leaves it armed, and its body finds a flag and returns. That is exactly the shape slash-commands-§7 forbids. Every other timer goes through AceTimer and StandDown's CancelAllTimers (:151-155). Because cleanupDone=true is set before the timer, retention is also skipped until the next session (review F-009).
findings.remediation: Audit (BL-46): schedule through NS.addon:ScheduleTimer(fn, 5) (or keep a C_Timer.NewTimer handle) so NS.StandDown cancels it. Keep the IsStoodDown belt, and clear cleanupDone on cancel or document the skip. Review (C-07): move the latch inside the timer with a session-only cleanupPending flag in core/State.lua, so a stand-down postpones rather than cancels. Retry on the next PEW. Combine the two: an AceTimer-armed prune plus the latch set only when the prune runs. Add a falsification case ('stand-down inside the prune window postpones rather than cancels'; red under C_Timer.After), +1 test. Update docs/performance.md:47. Smoke test C-07. Do this after R-06, the mock fix.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (every timer is canceled, not left armed to find a flag); testing-§12

verification.reason: core/BankLedger.lua:216-229 sets NS.State.cleanupDone=true at :218, before the C_Timer.After(5) at :220, and the body only checks NS.IsStoodDown (:225). C_Timer.After returns no handle, so StandDown's CancelAllTimers (:151) cannot reach it. slash-commands-§7 'What MUST stand down' says every timer is canceled, 'not left armed to wake up and find a flag'. That is exactly this shape, and the comment at :221-224 concedes it. Setting the latch before the timer also means a disable inside the 5 s window skips retention for the rest of the session. The combined remediation (an AceTimer-scheduled prune, with the latch set only when the prune runs) is correct, and so is the docs/performance.md:47 update. Low severity fits.

findings.title: A weapon-enchant (WPN_ENCH) macro deferred in combat is flushed as a single-item macro, losing /use 16 and /use 17 and the off-hand line
findings.evidence: A per-hand write queued in combat stores only itemID = mhPick or ohPick, and entry.cat is nil. FlushPending then rebuilds it through M.SetMacro, which only knows the single-item shape. A scratch probe gave '#showtooltip / /use item:944001 / /use 16 / /use item:944002 / /use 17' out of combat, but '#showtooltip / /use item:944003' after a deferral and flush. The fingerprint stores the wrong body, so nothing corrects it until some later recompute. Reachable through /cm rewritemacros in combat (documented as allowed), a weapon swap mid-fight, or an oil looted or used up mid-fight. The FlushPending test covers KCM_FOOD only.
findings.remediation: C-01: FlushPending replays the queued body. Composites keep pcall(M.SetCompositeMacro, entry.cat, nil). Every other entry calls pcall(commitMacro, name, entry.body, entry.itemID, entry.catKey) through the one write tail, with no second write path (events-frames-taint-§4). Characterization first (the FOOD case at :330), then two red-first cases: a per-hand flush keeps /use 16 and /use 17, and /cm rewritemacros in combat keeps the WPN_ENCH body. About +2 cases; regenerate test-cases.md and the badge.

verification.reason: The defect is real. modules/MacroManager.lua:411-420 queueForCombat stores body, itemID and catKey, and leaves cat nil for non-composites. SetWeaponEnchantMacro (:525-532) passes iconItemID = mhPick or ohPick. FlushPending (:598-602) sends every non-composite through M.SetMacro(name, entry.itemID, entry.catKey), and that rebuilds the body with BuildBody as a single-item body (:505-519). commitMacro then fingerprints that wrong body (:486-491). The only flush test (tests/test_macromanager.lua:330) covers KCM_FOOD. I lowered severity from high to medium. The damage lasts only until the next recompute: RecomputeOne (core/ConsumableMaster.lua:127-134) rebuilds the per-hand body, and alreadyApplied sees that lastBody differs, so any later bag or equipment event rewrites the macro. Nothing runs a recompute on regen itself, so the broken macro can last into the next pull if nothing else fires. It is a real but self-healing breakage, not a persistent one. The remediation (replay entry.body through commitMacro, with composites unchanged) is sound and keeps a single write tail.

Database:Init (854-906) and OnProfileChanged (805-829) re-run FoldLegacyUnits, BackfillLabelStyle, MigrateSpecKeys and BuildSpells, and nothing else. Init's own comment (lines 885-889) states this exact per-account vs per-profile trap for spell keys and fixes it only for MigrateSpecKeys. Any other profile keeps the hybrid array+keyed colors, which read back as the defaults, and keeps "NONE" font flags, which leave the outline dropdown blank. The remediation is sound: both steps are idempotent, and the keyed-vs-default guard stops stale array values from overwriting colors a user edited after the upgrade. walk() already tolerates a nil profile, so the extra guard only protects against a nil db. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:390 is the register row to update. I kept the severity because this is silent loss of saved customisation for every multi-profile user who upgraded.

findings.title: The Spells page HookScripts AceGUI's pooled Label and Dropdown frames, so its tooltips and mouse capture leak into every AceGUI consumer
findings.evidence: label.frame:EnableMouse(true) plus HookScript OnEnter/OnLeave, and dd.frame:HookScript('OnEnter', ...) showing the 'Category for future filtering…' tooltip. AceGUI recycles these frames through one process-global pool, a hook cannot be removed, and the Label and Dropdown OnAcquire reset neither scripts nor EnableMouse. Recycled labels in other addons' panels (AbsorbTracker, AuraMaster, BankLedger, ConsumableMaster, LootHistory, PanelMaster, PrettyChat) then show a KickCD spell tooltip and swallow clicks. One more hook pair is added per row per render, and F-008 doubles the renders. No test covers this.
findings.remediation: C-02: use AceGUI:Create('InteractiveLabel') with SetCallback OnEnter/OnLeave, which Release clears; call SetHighlight(nil) if the highlight is unwanted. For the dropdown, use H.AttachTooltip(dd, L['Category'], ...). Test: render twice, release, acquire a Label, and assert it has no KickCD OnEnter script and IsMouseEnabled() is false. The M2-T2 task can run in parallel with M2-T1.

verification.reason: settings/Spells.lua:662-666 is real. label.frame:EnableMouse(true) plus HookScript OnEnter/OnLeave on a pooled AceGUI Label, and the Label OnAcquire (libs/AceGUI-3.0/widgets/AceGUIWidget-Label.lua:72) resets neither the scripts nor mouse enabling. The AceGUI pool is process-global, so a recycled Label in another addon shows a stale KickCD spell tooltip and catches mouse input. The dropdown evidence is wrong, though. AceGUIWidget-DropDown.lua:647 creates the outer .frame as a plain Frame that is never mouse-enabled; mouse input goes to the child button and button_cover (lines 699 and 708). The dd.frame HookScript at Spells.lua:763-770 therefore never fires. Its tooltip is dead in KickCD today, and the cross-addon leak there is only latent. The impact is a cosmetic tooltip and hover glitch in other addons' panels, with no data or taint consequence, so the severity drops to medium. options-ui-§1 says nothing about hooking pooled frames; the closest standards anchor is the process-global-AceGUI reasoning of AP #76, applied here by analogy. The fix is correct: InteractiveLabel with SetCallback, and O.AttachTooltip (OptionsWidgets.lua:1094, which uses SetCallback on AceGUI widgets) for the dropdown. Release clears both.
verification.corrected_remediation: Replace the Label with AceGUI:Create('InteractiveLabel') and use SetCallback('OnEnter'/'OnLeave'). Call SetHighlight(nil) if the highlight is unwanted. Replace the dd.frame HookScript with H.AttachTooltip(dd, L['Category'], L['Category for future filtering. Currently informational only.']). This also fixes the dropdown tooltip, which never fires today because dd.frame is not mouse-enabled. Test: render twice, release, acquire a plain Label, and assert it has no OnEnter script and IsMouseEnabled() is false. Also assert the dropdown's OnEnter callback shows the tooltip. Drop the options-ui-§1 rule_ref, or cite AP #76 by analogy (AceGUI objects are process-global).

findings.title: Per-unit cast-event frames are rebuilt on every enable, leaking 36 frames per disable/enable cycle
findings.locations: core/Util.lua:437-445, modules/IconGrid.lua:810-822, modules/IconGrid.lua:831-832, modules/IconGrid.lua:860-861, modules/Castbar.lua:1016-1031, modules/Castbar.lua:1044-1045, modules/Castbar.lua:1109-1110, modules/Castbar.lua:1136
findings.evidence: Util.RegisterUnitCastEvent calls CreateFrame('Frame') per event: IconGrid makes 8 per unit and Castbar 10. DisableUnit and Suspend drop them with inst.eventFrames = {}. Scratch measurement: 142 -> 178 -> 214 -> 250 frames, +36 per cycle. Reached through /kcd disable+enable, the per-unit Enable toggles, a profile switch that flips enabled, and each /kcd perf suspend/resume. The helper also accepts any eventName, which is the shape of the forbidden 'general-purpose private-frame factory'. test_disabled counts registrations by name only, so it cannot see orphaned frames.
findings.remediation: Review C-03 / audit D1: hold one filter frame per (module, unit) on inst (Util.UnitCastFilter or Util.NewUnitFilter with Arm/Disarm), created once. Re-register events on EnableUnit/Resume and UnregisterAllEvents on teardown. Use a file-scope route map so enable allocates nothing (AP #43). Change the Resume guard at Castbar.lua:1136 to an armed flag. Narrow the helper to the cast family, or document its one job. Route the RegisterUnitEvent calls through the pcall-isolated helper (A-03). Test: CreateFrame count across two disable/enable cycles adds 0; it must be red on HEAD. Add a test_util idempotency case for Arm/Disarm. Update the per-unit frames paragraph in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

verification.reason: core/Util.lua:437-445 calls CreateFrame per event on every call. IconGrid.lua:810-822 registers 8 events per unit and Castbar.lua:1016-1031 registers 10. DisableUnit and Suspend (IconGrid.lua:831-832 and 860-861, Castbar.lua:1044-1045 and 1109-1110) unregister the frames and then drop them with eventFrames = {}. Castbar Resume (1136) keys the rebuild on #eventFrames == 0. Each cycle therefore orphans 18 frames per unit. events-frames-taint.md:22 says the filter frame MUST be re-used across a disable/enable cycle rather than rebuilt. slash-commands §7 (line 186) says the frame is unregistered and kept. Line 24 forbids a general-purpose private-frame factory, and RegisterUnitCastEvent takes any eventName. One caveat on the remediation: line 24 also bars a frame that picks up another event after it is created. The per-(module, unit) frame should register its fixed cast-family set, and later re-registration must only re-arm that same set.

findings.title: scheduleTimer returns nil (C_Timer.After), so the LibKa0s color-picker and slider throttle never engages
findings.evidence: `scheduleTimer = function(fn, delay) return _G.C_Timer.After(delay, fn) end`. The library uses the return value as its armed flag (libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:1471-1482), so every ~60 Hz drag tick schedules its own SetAndRefresh and CONFIG_CHANGED fan-out. No test pins the throttle's call count.
findings.remediation: C-04: `return _G.C_Timer.NewTimer(delay, fn)`. Test: drive the color widget's OnValueChanged 10 times inside one mock window and assert one SetAndRefresh. Independent of U-001 and can land early; U-001 makes it belt-and-braces.

verification.reason: settings/OptionsSetup.lua:243 returns the result of C_Timer.After, which is nil. libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:1472-1482 uses that return value as the armed flag (`if timer then return end`), and the slider drag throttle at 1329-1332 does the same. Both throttles therefore never coalesce, and every drag tick commits and fans out CONFIG_CHANGED. Switching to C_Timer.NewTimer returns a truthy handle, and the callback resets timer to nil. The fix is correct and local to the host.

findings.title: /kcd spells add disagrees with the Spells page: multi-word names split, Cooldown Manager gate skipped, resolver duplicated
findings.locations: core/KickCD.lua:501-505, core/KickCD.lua:570-584, core/KickCD.lua:617-624, settings/Spells.lua:272-285, settings/Spells.lua:461-473, README.md:95

The CLI skips cooldownManagerRejects, which the page applies, although the README says only tracked cooldowns can be added. The ID/name resolver exists twice. findings.title: Empowered casts (UNIT_SPELLCAST_EMPOWER_*) are not tracked by the cast bar or the icon grid's cast-state logic
findings.evidence: Neither module registers UNIT_SPELLCAST_EMPOWER_START/STOP/UPDATE (a grep for 'empower' finds nothing), while the sibling PartyFrameEnhanced does. The bar misses an empower started after targeting, may persist after one ends, and target_casting visibility and glow lag. Unverified in the client: it mainly affects PvP Evokers, and whether any NPC empowers is unknown.
findings.remediation: Part of C-03: add the three EMPOWER events to both route maps, riding the single filter frame. In Castbar they map to OnChannelStart/OnCastStop/OnCastDelayed, and in IconGrid to OnUnitCastEvent. Register them via pcall/C_EventUtils.IsEventValid. Add an EMPOWER note to docs/midnight-quirks.md. Verify with smoke test C-03 step 4; record it as untested if no Evoker is available.

verification.reason: A grep for 'empower' across core, modules and settings finds nothing. The route tables at Castbar.lua:1016-1027 and IconGrid.lua:810-819 have no UNIT_SPELLCAST_EMPOWER_START/UPDATE/STOP, while the sibling ../PartyFrameEnhanced/modules/CastBars.lua handles them. An Evoker empower started after targeting will not start the bar and is not cleared by its stop event. That is a real gap for an interrupt addon (empowers are interruptible, and PvP Evokers are common), but it can only be confirmed in the client. The remediation fits the fix for R-03, provided the EMPOWER events are part of the frame's fixed registration set at creation (events-frames-taint.md:24).

findings.title: An IconGrid rebuild repaints every icon 'ready' and relies on unordered CallbackHandler dispatch for correction
findings.evidence: BuildActiveList applies { ready = true, start = 0, duration = 0 } to every icon. Cooldowns and IconGrid both handle PEW, SPELLS_CHANGED, TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED, PROFILE_CHANGED and CONFIG_CHANGED, and dispatch runs in pairs order. If Cooldowns fires first, its SPELL_STATE lands on the old pool. An interrupt on cooldown can then show ready after a talent swap, pet summon, spec or profile switch, or /reload, until the next SPELL_UPDATE_*. Unverified in the client.
findings.remediation: C-06: publish a read-only Cooldowns:StateFor(spellID) returning watched[id]. After BuildActiveList, seed with btn:Apply(st or READY_SEED, true), where READY_SEED is a file-scope constant. Alternative: Cooldowns re-emits on GRID_LAYOUT. Test: register Cooldowns before IconGrid, fire PEW, and assert an on-cooldown icon is not ready. Serialize after R-03 (both touch IconGrid.lua). Smoke test C-06.

verification.reason: IconGrid.lua:351 seeds every rebuilt icon with { ready = true } and force=true. IconGrid (IconGrid.lua:934-941) and Cooldowns (Cooldowns.lua:547-555) both register PEW, spec change, SPELLS_CHANGED and TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED on AceEvent's shared CallbackHandler, which dispatches in pairs order. If Cooldowns:Rebuild runs first, its full SPELL_STATE emit (Cooldowns.lua:339) reaches the old pool, which is released right after. After that, Cooldowns:Refresh only emits on StateChanged (around 455-505), so an interrupt on cooldown can read 'ready' until its state next changes. IconGrid has no pull path from Cooldowns. It cannot be confirmed without the client, but the ordering hazard is real.

findings.title: Every Spells-page edit renders the page twice, and an error mid-render leaves the render guard stuck for the session
findings.evidence: doCommit calls RefreshRows and then FireConfigChanged, whose synchronous subscriber calls RefreshRows again. If fillRows raises, rebuildScheduled stays true and every later RefreshRows returns early. The comment's claim that the flag 'is cleared on EVERY exit' is true of the explicit returns only.
findings.remediation: C-07: doCommit only calls FireConfigChanged and lets the subscriber render, keeping the direct render only when NS.IsDown() (the subscriber is unregistered while disabled). Wrap the RefreshRows body so rebuildScheduled = false runs on a raise, then re-raise. Tests: one RefreshRows per commitSoon flush; after a forced fillRows raise, a later refresh renders.

verification.reason: The finding is real. doCommit (Spells.lua:404-407) calls RefreshRows and then FireConfigChanged. Helpers.FireConfigChanged (Panel.lua:144-156) sends synchronously outside a Coalesced batch, and the subscriber at Spells.lua:1345-1350 calls RefreshRows again, so the page renders twice. The two calls run sequentially, and the flag is cleared at 1243 between them, so the second render really happens. rebuildScheduled is set at 1182 and cleared only on the explicit returns (1189, 1236, 1243), so a raise in fillRows latches it for the session. The impact is small: one extra render of a short spell list per debounced edit, and the stuck flag needs an error in fillRows first. Medium overstates it, so it drops to low. slash-commands-§7 is not what is violated here. It only explains why the direct render must stay while NS.IsDown(): Spells.StandDown at 1422-1429 unregisters the subscriber. That part of the remediation is correct.
verification.corrected_remediation: doCommit should call only FireConfigChanged when the addon is up, and call RefreshRows directly only when NS.IsDown(), because StandDown has unregistered the CONFIG_CHANGED subscriber. Make RefreshRows run its body in a pcall/xpcall (or an equivalent) that always resets rebuildScheduled and then re-raises the error. Tests: one RefreshRows per commitSoon flush, and a later refresh still renders after a forced fillRows raise. Drop slash-commands-§7 as the rule_ref: this is a correctness defect, not a standards deviation.

findings.title: docs/performance.md's bucket table does not match the Perf descriptor, and spellState runs outside its declared stateEmit parent on the Rebuild path
findings.evidence: performance.md says spellState sits within spellPoll, omits stateEmit, and says glowGate is 'deliberately not declared'. PerfSetup declares stateEmit within spellPoll, spellState within stateEmit, and glowGate. The Rebuild emit at Cooldowns.lua:339 is not bracketed as stateEmit, and Perf.Note('spellState') at IconGrid.lua:994 passes no parent. The committed captures (20260909-014035) predate the current nesting.
findings.remediation: C-08: bracket Cooldowns' Rebuild emit as stateEmit (parent nil) so spellState always sits inside one. Regenerate the performance.md table from the descriptor. Add a test_perfsetup case that every spellState note has an open stateEmit under Perf.on. Re-check with tests/perf.lua, then take a two-arm in-game capture on 1.3.x and record it via /wow-addon:perf-analysis (smoke test C-08).

verification.reason: Real. docs/performance.md:36-55 lists spellState within spellPoll, has no stateEmit row, and says glowGate is 'deliberately not declared'. core/PerfSetup.lua:100-101,105 declares stateEmit within spellPoll, spellState within stateEmit, and glowGate. Cooldowns.lua:339 (Rebuild's SendMessage) has no bracket, while the Refresh emits at :452/:505 are bracketed as stateEmit with parent 'spellPoll'. IconGrid.lua:994 notes spellState with no parent. Severity goes down to low. The mis-nesting only happens on the Rebuild path, which runs on spell or spec changes and never per frame. The harm is a misleading nesting line in perf reports, not a runtime defect. The remediation also has a gap. If Rebuild's emit is bracketed as stateEmit with parent nil, stateEmit's own declared parent (within spellPoll) is still false on that path, because Rebuild never runs inside Cooldowns:Refresh. That moves the false claim up one level instead of removing it.
verification.corrected_remediation: Fix the Rebuild path so the declared nesting is true at every level. Either (a) bracket Rebuild's emit under its own undeclared or root bucket (e.g. 'rebuildEmit', no within) and have IconGrid:OnSpellState pass its observed parent to Perf.Note, so LibKa0s-Perf reports observedMixed honestly, or (b) drop stateEmit's 'within = spellPoll' and state in PerfSetup that stateEmit has two callers. Then regenerate the docs/performance.md bucket table from the PerfSetup descriptor, including stateEmit and glowGate and removing the 'glowGate not declared' paragraph. Add a test_perfsetup case asserting every spellState note happens under an open stateEmit and that stateEmit's observed parent matches its declaration. Re-run tests/perf.lua. The in-game two-arm capture via /wow-addon:perf-analysis stays as the smoke step.

findings.title: The High and Medium defects sit on paths no test covers, and the shared instance swallows an OnInitialize raise
findings.evidence:
The gaps:
- F-001: no profile swap at v5, and the mock AceDB has no SetProfile.
- F-002: no assertion on scripts or mouse state left on released widgets.
- F-003: mocks.__frames is never asserted.
- F-004: no throttle call count.
- F-008: no render count.
Also, tests/run.lua:105 runs pcall(NS.OnInitialize, NS), which hides an init raise.
findings.remediation: C-11: add a test per fix, each with a '-- red under:' line (testing-§12). Give tests/wow_mock.lua a real AceDB SetProfile; this is the addon's own mock, not the kit. Consider surfacing the OnInitialize pcall failure. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and move the README [tests] badge in each commit that adds a case (about +10-12 cases).

verification.reason: The coverage gap is real, but two pieces of evidence are wrong. (1) 'The mock AceDB has no SetProfile' is false. tests/wow_mock.lua:458 has SetProfile as a no-op stub copied onto every db, and tests/test_launcher.lua:344 calls it. The actual gap is that it does not swap profile data. (2) 'mocks.__frames is never asserted' is overstated. tests/test_disabled.lua:85 (shownFrames) and wow_mock.lua:531 (__registrationSet) both read it. What is missing is a frame-count assertion across a disable/enable cycle. tests/run.lua:105 does pcall(NS.OnInitialize, NS) and throws away the result, which is confirmed. tests/run.lua is the addon's own file, not tests/_kit, so routing locally is right. Missing tests are regression risk, not user-reachable impact, and the defects they cover are tracked separately (F-001..F-008), so the severity goes to low.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-11: add one red-under test per fix (testing-§12 '-- red under:' line). Replace the no-op SetProfile stub in tests/wow_mock.lua's DB_STUBS/AceDB mock with one that really switches db.profile to a separate per-profile table. That is the addon's own mock, not the kit. Add a #mocks.__frames delta assertion across disable/enable (F-003), plus a throttle call count (F-004) and a render count (F-008). Surface OnInitialize failures in tests/run.lua, either by capturing pcall's result and failing the instance or by not wrapping it. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and move the README tests badge in each commit that adds cases.

findings.title: Four stale or wrong code comments
findings.locations: core/KickCD.lua:13-19, core/KickCD.lua:23-27, modules/Cooldowns.lua:35-38, modules/Cooldowns.lua:648-650, core/Util.lua:101, settings/Spells.lua:1411
