findings.title: Three readers of the master 'enabled' path, one of which claims to be the only one; dead early returns in Cooldowns
findings.evidence: LifecycleSetup says it is 'THE one reader of the stored path', yet Cooldowns.isEnabled and Units.IsEnabled also read p.enabled. Cooldowns' Rebuild/Refresh early returns are dead under the latch.
findings.remediation: C-10: Cooldowns isEnabled -> NS.MasterEnabled; Units.IsEnabled uses NS.MasterEnabled() for its first rung. Drop the dead early returns, or comment that the latch is primary.

verification.reason: Real, but the finding undercounts. Besides core/LifecycleSetup.lua:59-71 (NS.MasterEnabled, 'THE one reader'), modules/Cooldowns.lua:298-302, and core/Units.lua:33-35, there is a fourth independent reader: modules/IconGrid.lua:133-136 isEnabled(), used at :190 and exported as IconGrid.MasterEnabled at :1343. Cooldowns also exports its copy as Cooldowns.MasterEnabled at :719. The Lifecycle latch exists in both the library and degraded-stub paths (LifecycleSetup.lua:146-175), so the Rebuild/Refresh early returns at Cooldowns.lua:311 and :408 are redundant under it. Direct calls from tests could still reach them.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-10: route all three module readers through NS.MasterEnabled(): Cooldowns isEnabled (:298), IconGrid isEnabled (:133), and Units.IsEnabled's first rung (:35). Keep the Cooldowns.MasterEnabled and IconGrid.MasterEnabled exports as aliases so callers don't break. Keep the early returns at Cooldowns.lua:311/:408 but comment them as defense-in-depth behind the latch, or drop them only if no test calls Rebuild/Refresh directly while disabled. After this change, LifecycleSetup's 'THE one reader' claim is true.

findings.title: README claims /kcd config opens after combat (the code refuses), and /kcd resetposition only resets the target icon grid
findings.evidence: README.md:97 says '/kcd config waits until combat ends' and :113 says 'it opens the moment combat ends'. NS:OpenSettings refuses and returns, which options-ui-§2 requires (MUST NOT defer-and-replay). Separately (review only), Helpers.ResetIconPosition resets only the target grid, while its help text says 'the icon grid'; the focus grid and both cast bars are untouched.
findings.remediation: Rewrite README :97 and :113: the game blocks the panel in combat, so run /kcd config again after it ends. Run the de-AI pass (documentation-§1). For resetposition, either extend ResetIconPosition to every unit's grid and rename the help text to 'Restore the icon grids to their default positions', or keep target-only and say so in the verb text. No badge moves.

verification.reason: README.md:97 ('/kcd config waits until combat ends') and :113 ('it opens the moment combat ends') contradict core/KickCD.lua:815-819, where NS:OpenSettings prints the combat notice and returns. The standard's combat gate (options-ui.md:76-78) forbids defer-and-replay, so the code is right and the README is wrong. Helpers.ResetIconPosition (settings/Panel_Render.lua:358-377) resets only units.target.anchors.icons, while the verb help at core/KickCD.lua:239 says 'Restore the icon grid to its default screen position'. That wording is ambiguous for two units with two grids and two cast bars. The remediation is documentation-only on the README side, and either option for resetposition is sound.

findings.title: GateHint probes by temporarily writing candidate values into the live profile
findings.evidence: `parent[key] = candidate` ... `parent[key] = gateVal` is a temporary write around the single write seam. It is safe only while every row.values() is pure and nothing runs in between.
findings.remediation: C-10: compute hints through row.valuesFor(gateValue) when present. Otherwise keep the probe, but go through Helpers.Resolve, restore in a pcall/finally shape, and document it as a read-only probe.

verification.reason: The temporary write is real: settings/Slash.lua:127-129 sets parent[key] = candidate, then pcall(allowedKeys, row), then parent[key] = gateVal. But most of the proposed remediation is already in place. The probe already resolves through H.Resolve (:122), already runs under pcall with an unconditional restore, and is already documented as a read-only probe (doc comment at :105-108, pinned by tests/test_color_shape.lua). Lua is single-threaded and nothing yields between write and restore, so the only reachable exposure is a row.values() with side effects. None is known. What remains is design hygiene.

findings.title: A disabled-at-login addon re-registers a PLAYER_LOGIN that will never fire
findings.evidence: `if not State.__seeded then boot:RegisterEvent('PLAYER_LOGIN') end` in State.StandUp. The first hold is taken inside PLAYER_LOGIN itself, so the 'enabled again before login' case cannot occur, and a dead registration is left behind.
findings.remediation: C-10: drop the PLAYER_LOGIN re-registration in State.StandUp; the InCombatLockdown() seed on the next line covers it. Coordinate with A-04 (the State boot frame may move to an AceEvent target).

verification.reason: core/State.lua:213 re-registers PLAYER_LOGIN when State.__seeded is unset. The only place the disabled hold is first taken is OnEnable (core/KickCD.lua:109, RefreshEnabledHold), and AceAddon runs OnEnable from its own PLAYER_LOGIN handler. AceAddon's frame registers at lib load (TOC line 21), which is before State.lua (line 55), so a disabled-at-login StandDown can release boot before boot's PLAYER_LOGIN is delivered. That leaves __seeded false, and a later /kcd enable re-registers an event that never fires again. The case the comment describes, 'disabled at load and enabled again before login', cannot happen, because no hold exists before PLAYER_LOGIN. The InCombatLockdown() seed on line 214 already covers the seed. No test references __seeded, so dropping the branch is safe. This is a harmless dead registration, so low is right.

Util.ResolveSpecID returns any number as-is (core/Util.lua:347-351). spellsAdd (core/KickCD.lua:617-630) passes both to Database:AddSpell (core/Database.lua:350), which calls EnsureSpellList (147-154) and creates profile.spells[CLASS][spec] with no validation. findings.title: LibKa0s OptionsWidgets uses the host's scheduleTimer return value as its armed flag; nil-returning hosts defeat the throttle
findings.evidence: The color throttle does `timer = d.scheduleTimer(...)` then `if timer then return end`, and the slider live-commit uses the same pattern. The Options.lua descriptor doc does not require a truthy handle. KickCD, LootHistory (settings/OptionsSetup.lua:205-207) and MultiMeters (settings/OptionsSetup.lua:270-272) all pass C_Timer.After wrappers that return nil.
findings.remediation: Upstream in LibKa0s: track armed in a library-local boolean set before calling d.scheduleTimer and cleared in the callback, and ignore the returned handle. Document in Options.lua that the return value is unused. Add a LibKa0s test with a nil-returning scheduleTimer asserting one commit per window. Bump the OptionsWidgets.lua LibStub minor (and Options.lua's if the file changes), update CHANGELOG, and tag. Then re-vendor the whole libs/LibKa0s and tests/_kit into KickCD and every consumer as its own commit, updating the CLAUDE.md provenance line; test_vendor_sync gates it. Never patch libs/ locally (library-stack-§7, #45/#48).

verification.reason: libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:1326-1337 (slider live commit: dragTimer = d.scheduleTimer(...); if dragTimer then return end) and 1471-1482 (color: timer = d.scheduleTimer(...)) both treat the host's return value as the armed flag. Options.lua:537-539 documents scheduleTimer(fn, delay) and says nothing about a return. KickCD settings/OptionsSetup.lua:243 returns C_Timer.After(...), which is nil. LootHistory settings/OptionsSetup.lua:205-207 and MultiMeters :270-272 return nothing. Every OnValueChanged during a drag therefore allocates a new closure and timer, and each timer commits the latest pending value, so the 50 ms throttle is defeated: roughly one commit per frame plus garbage. findings.rule_ref: events-frames-taint-§1 (MUST NOT create per-module frames for ordinary event traffic)

verification.reason: The defect is real. core/State.lua:143-146 is a CreateFrame boot frame carrying PLAYER_LOGIN and PLAYER_REGEN_*, and settings/Spells.lua:374-381 is a cacheEvents CreateFrame carrying TRAIT_CONFIG_UPDATED and PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED. Neither is a RegisterUnitEvent filter, so both breach the events-frames-taint-§1 MUST NOT. ARCHITECTURE.md:99 argues for the State frame, but the Documented deviations table (:376ff) has no row for it. The remediation has a load-order bug, though. NS.NewBusTarget is defined in core/KickCD.lua:46 (TOC line 68), and core/State.lua loads at TOC line 55, so calling NS.NewBusTarget() at State.lua file load would fail on a nil call. Moving cacheEvents onto Spells.__ev (settings/Spells.lua:1334) is fine, though __ev is created lazily inside ensure-panel code, so it has to be created eagerly at module scope for the invalidator to stay armed when the panel is never opened.
verification.corrected_remediation: Move cacheEvents onto an AceEvent target created eagerly at settings/Spells.lua module scope, via NS.NewBusTarget(), which is available by then, or a shared Spells.__ev created at file load rather than in the lazy panel builder, so the cache still invalidates when the panel is never opened. Then rewrite StandDown/StandUp as UnregisterAllEvents/RegisterEvent on that target. findings.title: Mythic+ keystone context never cleared; every later GameObject loot recorded as MPLUS
findings.evidence: State.keystone is set on CHALLENGE_MODE_START and deliberately kept after completion. It is cleared only in Attribution:Disable (:411); grep finds writes only at :229/:238/:411. ResolveLootSource maps any GameObject loot to S.MPLUS while state.keystone is set, so herbs, ore, world chests and other instances' containers are persisted to LootHistoryDB as MPLUS with a keystoneLevel. That pollutes the Source column and filter, the Insights by-source and keystone breakdowns (core/Database.lua:557-558) and both CSVs, with no repair. No test covers the context lifetime; only the pure resolver case at tests/test_attribution.lua:71 exists. Related, unverified: at :238 a completion-time 0 from GetActiveKeystoneLevel is truthy, so 0 would be stored.
findings.remediation: C-001: add a presence-guarded NS.Compat.InPartyInstance() shim (IsInInstance, instanceType == 'party'). Add Attribution:OnZoneChanged, which clears State.keystone when not in a party instance, and OnChallengeModeReset. Register ZONE_CHANGED_NEW_AREA and CHALLENGE_MODE_RESET on bus and append them to self.__events so Disable tears them down. Do NOT register PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD on NS.addon, which would collide with LifecycleSetup:112 OnEnterWorld. Guard :238 with (lvl and lvl > 0). Add 3 tests (clears when out of instance, kept in instance, CHALLENGE_MODE_RESET) and update the Enable 'seven events' case to nine. Update docs/data-flow.md:88 and midnight-quirks.md:22, and move test-cases.md and the badge in the same commit. Smoke S-001. Existing mislabelled rows cannot be repaired (no signal).

verification.reason: modules/Attribution.lua:174-176 maps any GameObject to MPLUS while state.keystone is set. The only writes to keystone are :229 (start), :238 (completion keeps it) and :411 (Disable). Nothing clears it on leaving the instance, and a grep of core/modules/settings finds no ZONE_CHANGED or CHALLENGE_MODE_RESET handler. So every herb, ore or chest looted later in the session is persisted as MPLUS, and that shows up in the Source column and filter and in Database.lua:557. :238 uses `or`, so a completion-time 0 would be stored. Enable registers 7 events (:346-359) and tests/test_attribution.lua:396 pins 'seven'. The remediation is sound: it keeps PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD off NS.addon, where LifecycleSetup.lua:112 already binds OnEnterWorld.

findings.title: Currency-category cache is built once per session and never rebuilt
findings.evidence: The id-to-header map is a snapshot taken at the session's first currency loot. A currency first discovered later, or one under a header that was collapsed at build time (unverified), is missing from it. Its row is persisted with itemSubType = nil and never backfilled. This hits routinely at season start.
findings.remediation: C-003: in Compat.CurrencyCategory, rebuild the cache once per miss-burst (sentinel __rebuiltFor, preferably held in a local) and re-look-up. The alternative is to nil the cache on CURRENCY_DISPLAY_UPDATE, but that adds a registration to the stand-down list, so rebuild-on-miss is preferred. Add a +1 case in tests/test_compat.lua where the mock list gains an id after the first call. Smoke S-003.

verification.reason: The defect is real. core/Compat.lua:390-393 builds currencyCategoryCache once and never invalidates it. A currency discovered after the first build misses, and Collector.lua:198 persists itemSubType=nil permanently, so the row falls out of the subtype filter (Database.lua:348). The remediation is incomplete for the collapsed-header case the finding itself raises. GetCurrencyListSize/GetCurrencyListInfo only enumerate children of expanded headers, so rebuild-on-miss cannot recover an id under a collapsed header. Also, tests/test_compat.lua:338 asserts that an unknown id returns nil, so a rebuild must not change that answer.
verification.corrected_remediation: In Compat.CurrencyCategory, rebuild the cache at most once per miss (a module-local sentinel keyed by the missed id, so an id that is genuinely absent does not trigger a walk on every loot) and look it up again. Keep the unknown-id -> nil contract (test_compat.lua:338). findings.title: Shortening 'Keep history for' deletes history immediately with no confirm
findings.evidence: The settings.retentionDays onChange calls NS.Database:PruneOld() directly. A mis-click in the dropdown, or /lh set settings.retentionDays 7, irreversibly drops older records in the same action. /lh purge, by contrast, goes through the KA0S_LOOTHISTORY_PURGE confirm. No test pins this onChange today.
findings.remediation: C-004: keep the Schema:Set write unchanged (architecture-§5). Add Database:CountOlderThan(days). If the count is 0, do nothing. Otherwise show a KA0S_LOOTHISTORY_PRUNE StaticPopup naming N: accept runs PruneOld; decline prints 'retention set; N older records will be removed at your next login.' and the existing deferred login prune applies it. Headless / no StaticPopup_Show keeps the immediate prune. Add +2 tests in tests/test_schema.lua (popup present defers, with a red-under comment; popup absent prunes). Update docs/settings-panel.md. Smoke S-004.

verification.reason: The behaviour is real. settings/Schema.lua:370-375 onChange calls NS.Database:PruneOld() immediately, so a dropdown mis-click or '/lh set settings.retentionDays 7' deletes older records with no confirm, while /lh purge is confirmed (Slash.lua:8-18). The rule_ref is wrong: options-ui.md §12 governs only the global reset act and its wording, not retention changes, so this is a UX/data-safety finding with no standards backing. The remediation's decline path only defers the deletion to the next login rather than preventing it, which is weak protection.
verification.corrected_remediation: Keep the Schema:Set write (architecture-§5). Add Database:CountOlderThan(days) and do nothing when it is 0. Otherwise show a KA0S_LOOTHISTORY_PRUNE StaticPopup naming N, following the house pair: Yes/No, timeout=0, whileDead, hideOnEscape. Accept runs PruneOld. Headless, or with no StaticPopup_Show, keep the immediate prune. Add tests in tests/test_schema.lua for popup present (no prune before accept, and decline restores) and popup absent (prunes). Update docs/settings-panel.md. Drop the options-ui-§12 rule_ref; there is no standards rule behind this.

findings.title: Degraded Slash stub refusal line drifted from lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT
findings.evidence: The stub renders '... enable it with /lh' while claiming to be byte-identical to the library, which renders '<brand> ... /lh enable'. That breaks the canonical refusal-line shape. On that path, enable itself is unavailable, so the line points at nothing that works. Reachable only on a library-less install with settings.enabled=false.
findings.remediation: C-005: format the stub line with '/lh enable' (slash .. ' enable'), and correct the comment to note that enable is unavailable on the library-less path. Better still, drop the stub's own format string. Add a +1 parity case in the degraded block of tests/test_slash.lua comparing the stub output to lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT:format(NS.BRAND, '/lh enable') with the library loaded. Smoke S-005. Re-check after any LibKa0s re-vendor in case the library format moved.

verification.reason: The drift is real. settings/Slash.lua:255-257 formats the line with '/lh', while the library (libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:596) passes slash..' enable'. The format string itself is identical to lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT (:83), so the 'byte-identical' comment is wrong about the argument, not the template. Severity lowered to low. It is reachable only on a library-less install, which cannot happen with the vendored payload, and it also needs settings.enabled=false. On that path, enable is in UNAVAILABLE_WITHOUT_LIB (:282-286), so neither '/lh' nor '/lh enable' leads anywhere that works. The fix is a parity and comment correction only.

findings.title: AH priority list re-parsed per record on every Stats/export pass; accumulateTime calls date() twice per record
findings.evidence: AuctionPrice:Pick calls cfg() and runs tag:match('^(.-):(.+)$') on each priority tag, up to 11 allocating matches per record. It is reached once per record in Database:Stats and 3-4 times per CSV row. accumulateTime calls date() twice per record, and date('*t') allocates a table. Both violate the loop-invariant hoist rule stated at core/Database.lua:307-313. Unverified: there is no perf runner or capture.
findings.remediation: C-006 steps 1-2: add a module-local compiled plan {prov,key,tag} rebuilt by AuctionPrice:RefreshPlan() from ReconcilePriority, from MovePriorityWithin (tail call only, no new branch: it is at CCN 15) and on SETTINGS_CHANGED, via a new bus target that joins the stand-down list. Pick walks the plan with no match or cfg(). Add a per-Stats-call dayCache keyed ts//86400, keeping date('*t') for the hour. Add a test that Pick honors a reorder after MovePriorityWithin. Take an M3.0 baseline with an uncommitted micro-benchmark and smoke S-006. Claim no numbers that were not measured.

verification.reason: The code shape is real. AuctionPrice:Pick (modules/AuctionPrice.lua:91-100) calls cfg() and tag:match per priority tag for each record. It is reached per record from Util.RecordValue in Database:Stats and 3 times per CSV row (Export.lua:96-100). accumulateTime (Database.lua:534-539) calls date() twice. The rule_ref is misapplied: events-frames-taint.md §7 governs per-frame loops (OnUpdate/OnEvent), and Stats and Export are user-initiated, not per-frame. The Database.lua:307-313 comment scopes its hoist rule to QueryList. Nothing was measured, so severity is low. The proposed fix (a compiled plan, a new SETTINGS_CHANGED bus target, and an addition to the stand-down list) adds a registration and invalidation surface out of proportion to an unmeasured cost.
verification.corrected_remediation: Measure first with an uncommitted micro-benchmark over a large synthetic history, and act only if it shows a real cost. If it does, memoize tag parsing in a module-local table keyed by the tag string (tag -> prov, key). Tag strings are immutable, so this needs no invalidation, no bus target and no stand-down change. In Stats/Export, read cfg() once per call and pass the priority list to Pick (for example Pick(map, priority)). For accumulateTime, cache the day string per ts//86400 within one Stats call. Add a test that Pick honours a reorder after MovePriorityWithin. Drop the events-frames-taint-§7 rule_ref.

findings.title: Event-registration blocks are not isolated per event and nothing records rejected event names
findings.locations: modules/Attribution.lua:349-355, modules/Attribution.lua:369, modules/Collector.lua:218-219, modules/Browser.lua:1246, modules/Browser.lua:1252, core/LifecycleSetup.lua:112
findings.evidence: Every registration is a bare call. A retired event name would raise, and every registration after it in the block would go unbound silently. A grep for IsEventValid, __badEvents or rejected in core, modules and settings finds nothing. This is latent: every name is valid on 12.1. The C_EventUtils.IsEventValid SHOULD is also unmet.
findings.remediation: Add NS.SafeRegister(target, event, handler, unit), which front-gates with C_EventUtils.IsEventValid and pcalls the register, plus NS.RejectedEvents, in core/LifecycleSetup.lua or core/Util.lua. Route every block through it. Keep Attribution.__events as the names that actually registered, so Disable stays symmetric. Surface the list via /lh debug events and a clause in the [Init] summary. Add C_EventUtils to .luacheckrc. Test with the kit's M.__badEvents (ENCOUNTER_START): the other six still register and the rejected list names it. tests/test_disabled.lua must still reach an empty set. Smoke S2.

verification.reason: The cited code matches. Attribution.lua:349-355 has seven bare bus:RegisterEvent calls and :369 has a bare RegisterUnitEvent. Collector.lua:218-219, Browser.lua:1246/1252 and LifecycleSetup.lua:112 are also bare. A grep of core/, modules/ and settings/ finds no IsEventValid, rejected-list or pcall guard. The rule is events-frames-taint-§1 ('An unknown event name raises...', standards/events-frames-taint.md). It requires a MUST for per-event pcall isolation and a MUST that rejected names are recorded and reachable from the debug verb or console. The IsEventValid front-gate is a SHOULD, so the finding reads the rule correctly. All current names are valid, so the defect is latent and low is right. No LibKa0s module provides a safe-register helper; I grepped libs/LibKa0s. An addon-local helper is therefore correct, and it is not the forbidden frame factory because it creates no frames. The kit mock supports M.__badEvents (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725), so the proposed test works. Also note the event-to-edge trade in the quirks doc, as §1 says.

findings.title: Vendored runner always records the perf skip as 'no tests/perf.lua', never the ratified performance-§12 exemption

Add kit cases for with-row, without-row, and unparseable register (fails loudly). Release a tag, re-vendor the whole of LibKa0s (libs/LibKa0s + tests/_kit, provenance line and +x bit in the same commit) with its own docs/revendor bundle, then run the four suites so the new bundle records reason (2). LibKa0s testkit/run-automated-tests.sh (HEAD 46ccaa6) has only the same negative wording at :841. The fix therefore belongs upstream in LibKa0s, followed by a whole re-vendor, as the finding says.

findings.title: schemaVersion held at 1 in defaults while migrations stamp to 8, reasoned only in a comment

The comment gives a real reason (a seeded stamp would claim migrations that never ran under the AceDB backfill), and open-evolutions records this as the unruled 'Migration-stamp ownership' case. The rule conflicts with the runner shape savedvariables-§1 prints.
findings.remediation: Local: add a versioning-git register row citing the comment and open-evolutions 'Migration-stamp ownership', with trigger 'the standard rules on migration-stamp ownership'. Upstream (WowAddonStandards, not blocking): propose that versioning-git defer to the migration-stamp ruling, or state that the runner's highest 'to' is the version and the defaults value is the pre-migration floor. This resolves the conflict with savedvariables-§1.

verification.reason: defaults/Global.lua:6-13 holds schemaVersion = 1 with the floor rationale in a comment; core/Database.lua MIGRATIONS ladder reaches to = 8 (:103) and RunMigrations (:127-138) stamps per step. versioning-git.md:8 MUST 'increment schemaVersion (in defaults) whenever a SV migration is required'; savedvariables.md:18-24 prints the runner shape starting from g.schemaVersion or 1; open-evolutions.md:15 carries 'Migration-stamp ownership' as open. findings.title: 'Always show yourself' does nothing on the default profile (maxRows=0): the pin works against a 40-row cap, but the window draws only about 10 rows
findings.evidence: ApplyRowLimit treats cap<=0 as Const.MAX_ROWS (40), while Render stops at layout.maxRows (10 at 220px). The pin also ignores the scroll offset. Headless repro: 'default window: maxRows=0 alwaysShowSelf=true visible=10 kept=20 self-in-view=false' (player at rank 15). The existing test covers only an explicit maxRows=3.
findings.remediation: C-02: add a pure, allocation-free Aggregator.SelfPinIndex(entries, first, visible, rowsConfig) beside ApplyRowLimit. Window:Render computes the pin index for 1+offset and layout.maxRows (skipped in drill-down) and draws entries[pin] in the last slot. Keep ApplyRowLimit's pin. Keep Render at CCN 15 or below with a single-expression substitution or a named local, never a part2 split. Pass the entry's real rank if the name cell shows one. Tests: 3 in tests/test_window.lua (default window with player at rank 15; scrolled so the player is in the slice; alwaysShowSelf=false) and 1 in tests/test_aggregator.lua. Smoke test SM-04.

verification.reason: Aggregator.lua:1291-1311 maps maxRows<=0 to Const.MAX_ROWS (40, Constants.lua:616) and pins the player at rows[40]. Window.lua:328-335 rowCapacity derives layout.maxRows from the frame height, and Render at Window.lua:1206-1207 stops at layout.maxRows starting from 1+offset. No other pin exists in Window*.lua (grep for isPlayer). Defaults.lua:281 has alwaysShowSelf=true, so on the default profile a player ranked past the visible rows is never pinned. In raids this is common and silent, so high stands. The remediation is sound.

findings.title: A disabled addon re-shows its windows when Test mode is unticked, because WindowProto:Show() skips the latch
findings.evidence: The guard at :659 checks only NS.Perf.suspended (the perf hold) and never NS.IsStoodDown(). WindowProto:Show() calls frame:Show() without consulting NS.ShouldShow. Headless repro: 'windows shown while disabled after test-mode on/off: 1 / 1'. The window stays up because every event is unregistered.
findings.remediation: C-01: WindowProto:Show() returns false first when NS.IsStoodDown(). Change WindowManager.lua:659 to use `not (NS.IsStoodDown and NS.IsStoodDown())`. Test in tests/test_disabled.lua: disable mid-session, tick and untick Test mode, and assert no window is shown ('red under' reverting the Show() guard). Keep test_lifecycle.lua:288 and Disabled 5 green. Smoke test SM-01.

verification.reason: WindowManager.lua:659 passes keepShown = not enabled and not NS.Perf.suspended, so it never checks NS.IsStoodDown(). applyTestMode (:630) then calls inst:Show(). Window_Placement.lua:231-242 WindowProto:Show() calls frame:Show() and sets forcedShow with no latch check. The settings panel's state.testMode setter (Schema_Compose.lua:794-801) reaches M:SetTestMode while disabled. NS.IsStoodDown (LifecycleSetup.lua:270) covers both the disabled hold and the perf hold, so the proposed :659 change subsumes the current perf check. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: Chat exports call the deprecated global SendChatMessage from a feature module, and would silently fall back to printing to self
findings.evidence: `local send = chatType and _G.SendChatMessage`. The global has been deprecated since 11.2.0 (Deprecated_ChatInfo.lua) in favour of C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage. When it is absent, the export prints the lines to the player and returns true, with no notice, so a channel export looks sent when nothing was sent.
findings.remediation: C-03: add Compat.ChatSender() in core/Compat.lua, resolved at call time, preferring C_ChatInfo.SendChatMessage and falling back to _G.SendChatMessage. Export.lua uses NS.Compat.ChatSender(). If a real channel was requested and no sender exists, print one localized notice before the self-print. SELF stays silent. Tests (tests/test_export.lua): C_ChatInfo preferred; one notice on RAID with no sender; no notice on SELF. A LibKa0s-Compat member is deferred (one consumer, anti-pattern #55). Smoke test SM-05.

verification.reason: Export.lua:879 does `chatType and _G.SendChatMessage` in a feature module, and :885-889 silently self-prints when it is absent. compat.md:5/25 does make Compat.lua the only file allowed to call deprecated APIs, so the deviation is real. Severity is lowered to medium: the global still resolves through Blizzard's deprecation fallbacks today, so no export fails now. The silent fallback is a future-removal risk, not live breakage. The remediation is fine.

findings.title: During a perf capture's suspended arm, /mm toggle and the launcher's left-click still show windows
findings.evidence: Feature verbs are refused only while disabled. Under the perf hold, Toggle calls inst:Show(), which bypasses the ladder. Headless repro: 'windows shown during perf suspend after /mm toggle: 1 / 1'. This contaminates arm B of the capture.
findings.remediation: C-01: the Show() latch guard, plus M:Toggle returning false with L['Windows are suspended while a performance capture runs.'] when NS.IsStoodDown(). The launcher (LauncherSetup.lua:235-236) prints that err. Add the locale key. Test in tests/test_disabled.lua: under a perf suspend, toggle and launcher onClick show nothing and print the line. Smoke test SM-02.

verification.reason: The Slash gate asks only NS.IsDisabled (Slash.lua:254; the comment at :150 says so), and the launcher's onClick (LauncherSetup.lua:229-237) does the same. Under a perf suspend, M:Toggle (WindowManager.lua:690-708) calls inst:Show(), and Show() bypasses NS.ShouldShow's step-0 latch. That puts a shown, redrawing window into the suspended arm, against performance-§6. The remediation is correct. Using IsStoodDown for the refusal while keeping the IsDisabled-based gate wording separate matches the design in LifecycleSetup.lua:277.

findings.title: A window created while the addon is stood down is armed with an OnUpdate
findings.evidence: Window.New calls inst.frame:SetScript('OnUpdate', onUpdate) unconditionally. Create and Duplicate are reachable from the settings panel while disabled. Reproduced headless: the OnUpdate is left armed.
findings.remediation: C-01: arm OnUpdate only when not NS.IsStoodDown(). Stand-up already re-arms it via WindowManager:Resume. Test: Create while disabled leaves no OnUpdate, and after enable every instance has one. Smoke test SM-03.

verification.reason: Window.lua:1382 arms OnUpdate unconditionally in Window.New, and Create/Duplicate (WindowManager.lua:253, :341) can call it while stood down. That breaks slash-commands.md:190/279 ('no new one is armed for the rest of the run'), so the finding is real. Severity is lowered because RefreshVisibility at :1383 hides the frame (ShouldShow step 0), and WoW does not fire OnUpdate on a hidden frame. There is no CPU cost unless something shows the frame, which is R-02/R-04's defect. It is a standards deviation with nil reachable impact once C-01 lands. The remediation is fine.

findings.title: The Slash degradation stub has no DisabledLine, and the launcher calls it through an always-present wrapper
findings.evidence: The wrapper `function Sl:DisabledLine() return cli:DisabledLine() end` always exists, so the launcher's guard passes and the stub raises 'attempt to call method DisabledLine' on a disabled left-click. This is reachable only when Launcher loads and Slash does not.
findings.remediation: C-04: publish Sl:DisabledLine only if cli.DisabledLine exists. Do not add a separate stub wording. Test in tests/test_degraded.lua: remove LibKa0s-Slash from libFiles, disable, call the launcher onClick, and assert no error and no write. Optionally note the coverage in test_surface_parity's header. Smoke test SM-11.

verification.reason: The stub's SlashLib:New (Slash.lua:185-236) builds no DisabledLine. The wrapper at :743 always exists, so the launcher's `Sl.DisabledLine` guard (LauncherSetup.lua:232) passes and cli:DisabledLine errors. That is real. It is reachable only when the vendored LibKa0s-Slash fails to load while the Launcher loads, and the addon is disabled, and the player left-clicks. That is a degradation-path edge case, so low rather than medium. The remediation is fine.

findings.title: Every refresh releases and rebuilds every visible row, and Row:Update writes hidden cells
findings.locations: modules/Window.lua:1168; modules/Window.lua:912-914; modules/Window.lua:1206-1220; modules/Row.lua:1446-1455; modules/Row.lua:1199-1204; modules/Row.lua:1376-1378
findings.evidence: HideAll releases the pool and Cell:Clear clears each cell. Rows are then re-acquired, re-anchored and refilled 4 times a second in combat. Capture 20260909-014604 (dated, solo): render 0.75 ms/pass, renderRow 0.10 ms/row. Offline refresh20x7 is 1.31 ms/iter. The saving is unmeasured.
findings.remediation: C-05 (measure first): keep self.slots bound across passes, acquire only when needed, release only the surplus, and re-anchor only when layoutVersion (bumped in ApplyConfig) changes. Row:Update iterates self.live instead of pairs(self.cells). Row.lua must stay at or under 1500 lines. Gate: before and after in-client /mm perf bundles (SM-07) with render ms/call lower. Offline refresh20x7 must keep API count at 8 and bytes/iter at or under 303438.1. Revert if render does not move.

verification.reason: The churn is real: Render calls HideAll -> Pool.ReleaseAll -> Row:Release, which clears every cell (Row.lua:1446-1455, Window.lua:912-914, :1168). Row:Update also iterates pairs(self.cells) (Row.lua:1376-1378), including cells that ApplyLayout hid. The remediation's reference to an existing `self.live` is wrong, though. `live` is a per-call local in RowProto:ApplyLayout (Row.lua:1311-1326) and is never stored on the row. The saving is also explicitly unmeasured and gated on in-client captures, so low rather than medium. Row.lua is currently 1469 lines, which leaves 31 lines of headroom under the 1500 cap.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-05 (measure first): keep self.slots bound across passes, acquire only when needed, release only the surplus, and re-anchor only when layoutVersion (bumped in ApplyConfig) changes. For Row:Update, make ApplyLayout keep an ordered array of live cells on the row (self.liveCells, rebuilt only in ApplyLayout, reusing the table rather than allocating a new one each call). Row:Update then iterates that array instead of pairs(self.cells). The alternative is to iterate layout.columns and index self.cells. Row.lua must stay at or under 1500 lines. Gate: before and after in-client /mm perf bundles (SM-07) with render ms/call lower. Offline refresh20x7 must keep API count at 8 and bytes/iter at or under 303438.1. Revert if render does not move.

findings.title: The remembered roster (db.global.roster) is persisted with no bound and is never cleared at login
findings.locations: modules/Roster.lua:355-361; modules/Roster.lua:572-582; modules/Roster.lua:621; modules/Roster.lua:628-630; modules/Roster.lua:489; modules/Roster.lua:506; modules/Roster.lua:519
findings.evidence: Every build() records each member into seenMap.byGuid, which is cleared only by Roster.Forget on METER_RESET. IsGroupMember falls back to the remembered map, so players from earlier sessions may pass the group filter. Unverified: whether DAMAGE_METER_RESET fires at login.
findings.remediation: C-14, blocked on smoke test SM-06. If the meter is empty after a fresh login, call Roster.Forget() on ENTERING_WORLD with isLogin. If the data survives logout, cap the map (for example, prune entries not in the live roster above 4 x MAX_ROWS). Add a case in either branch. No SavedVariables write from a game event while disabled.

verification.reason: Roster.lua:355-361 copies each member into db.global.roster.byGuid. That map is cleared only by Roster.Forget (:572-582) on METER_RESET (:621, :628-630), and IsGroupMember/OwnerOf fall back to it (:506, :519). So the map is persisted with no bound, as stated. The impact is speculative, though. A remembered GUID matters only if it appears in the current C_DamageMeter session data, which is group-scoped. Growth is bounded by the players you grouped with between meter resets. The finding itself says the login behaviour is unverified and blocks on SM-06. That makes it SavedVariables hygiene at low, not medium. The remediation, conditional on SM-06, is sound.

findings.title: Visibility:Evaluate runs the whole ladder to feed a LastResult cache that no shipped code reads
findings.evidence: Visibility.LastResult has zero callers in core/, modules/ or settings/. Only a test reads it. Each window's rules are evaluated twice per context edge, with a table allocated per changed result.
findings.remediation: C-06: return early from Evaluate when not State.debug, and delete Visibility.LastResult and its test (or wire it into /mm debug diag). Keep the subscriptions.

verification.reason: modules/Visibility.lua:373 defines LastResult. A grep of core/, modules/ and settings/ finds no caller, and only tests/test_visibility.lua:451,459,493,498 read it. Evaluate (:389-419) runs ShouldShow for every window and allocates a table in remember() on each change. It does this on ZONE, ENTERING_WORLD, ROSTER, COMBAT and PLAYER_STATE edges (:461-471), and modules/Window.lua:1292-1313 subscribes to the same edges and runs the ladder again. Evaluate publishes nothing, so outside debug the pass has no effect. Side note: core/LifecycleSetup.lua:102-106 says standDownVisibility's Refresh is 'the pass that asks them [windows] to go', but Evaluate hides nothing. That comment is wrong whether or not this fix lands. Callers ignore Refresh's return value (LifecycleSetup:106,173, Schema_Compose:58), so an early return is safe.

findings.title: Window commands answer with the wrong error string
findings.locations: modules/WindowManager.lua:704; modules/WindowManager.lua:272; modules/WindowManager.lua:307; modules/WindowManager.lua:309; modules/WindowManager.lua:324; modules/WindowManager.lua:471-472; locales/enUS.lua:901
findings.evidence: /mm toggle <unknown> answers 'Setting not found: %s'. /mm window delete|copy <unknown> answers 'No window is selected.' An empty rename answers the label L['Window name'].

Delete :272 and CopyFrom :471-472 return 'No window is selected.' for an unknown name, and Slash.lua reaches these through WINDOW_VERBS (Delete(tail), CopyFrom(source,target)). Rename :309 returns L['Window name'] for an empty name. The rule_ref is wrong, though. These strings are already routed through L, and localization-§2 (English source-of-truth keys) is met. verification.corrected_remediation: Same as C-07, with rule_ref cleared: this is not a localization-§2 deviation.

findings.title: Feature-verb acknowledgements are raw English strings, with a concatenated plural
findings.locations: settings/Slash.lua:415; settings/Slash.lua:428; settings/Slash.lua:446-447; settings/Slash.lua:580; settings/Slash.lua:632-633; settings/Slash.lua:696-697
findings.evidence: These lines are unrouted, while the same file routes NS.L["No window named '%s'."] at :574. The plural is built by concatenation.
findings.remediation: C-08: route every one through L[...] with English keys, using two keys for the plural. Add them to locales/enUS.lua and leave no enUS key unread. Smoke test SM-09.

verification.reason: The cited raw strings exist: settings/Slash.lua:415 (lock), :428 (test), :446-447 (reset positions, where the plural is built by concatenating '1 window'/'N windows'), :580, :632-633 (feign) and :696-697 (tooltip). :574 routes NS.L. The rule refs are wrong. The routing SHOULD, and the note that concatenated sentences are unroutable, are in localization-§1. §2 covers English keys, and §3 covers enUS coverage plus the English-only register. MultiMeters has no documented-deviation row that puts it in the English-only state (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:414 only mentions 'English only' as a ceiling), so the SHOULD is open. The same file has more unrouted user-facing lines that the finding misses: :193/:207 (version), :232 ('unknown command'), :367, :556 and WINDOW_USAGE at :453-455.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-08: route the cited lines through NS.L with whole-sentence English keys and format placeholders, using two keys for the 1/N windows plural. Do the same for the other unrouted user-facing lines in settings/Slash.lua (:193, :207, :232, :367, :556, WINDOW_USAGE). Add every key to locales/enUS.lua and leave no enUS key unread. Cite localization-§1 (routing SHOULD), not §2/§3. Smoke test SM-09.

findings.title: Stale and misplaced comments on the show ladder, spell and system handlers, load order and launcher

findings.title: The test mock hard-codes Version='0.1.0', so perf records carry the wrong version
findings.evidence: The TOC says 1.0.0, but perf.json records "version":"0.1.0".
findings.remediation: C-10: derive Version from the MultiMeters.toc '## Version:' line through the mock's root, not a hard-coded value. Move any case asserting 0.1.0 in the same commit.

findings.title: .luacheckrc whitelists the removed global GetSpellInfo
findings.evidence: The code calls only Compat.GetSpellInfo (modules/DrillDown.lua:549-550, modules/Tooltip_Lines.lua:660-661). A future bare call would lint clean.
findings.remediation: C-11: remove 'GetSpellInfo' from read_globals, then confirm luacheck is still 0/0.

Outside libs/ and docs, the only bare mentions are comments and mock-table field writes in tests/test_compat.lua (m.GetSpellInfo, C_Spell = { GetSpellInfo = ... }). findings.title: docs/performance.md quotes a feign figure (71224.1) that the runner no longer produces (71544.1)
findings.evidence: Today's tests/perf.lua gives feignTraceAbsent and feignTraceOff at 71544.1 each.
findings.remediation: C-12: re-run tests/perf.lua in the commit and quote the printed figure, keeping the arm-equality claim. Never hand-edit a number without the run.

verification.reason: The mismatch is real. I ran tests/perf.lua today and it prints feignTraceAbsent and feignTraceOff at 71544.1 each, while docs/performance.md:289-290 says 71224.1. The doc frames that figure as a historical record, though: 'On the run that closed this, both arms measured 71224.1 bytes/iter exactly, against 77944.1 and 71224.1 before the fix.' A dated measurement of a past run is not drift. Swapping in today's figure would also mix runs, because the before-fix pair cannot be reproduced. The claim that matters, equality between the arms, still holds. That makes this info, not low.
verification.corrected_remediation: C-12: keep the historical sentence and label it as the closing run's figures. If a current figure is wanted, re-run tests/perf.lua in the commit and add today's printed value (71544.1 for both arms as of 2026-09-23) as a separate, dated statement that keeps the arm-equality claim. findings.title: The drill-down closes when its window is renamed
findings.evidence: The drill-down exits on any WINDOWS_CHANGED addressed to its window, including action 'renamed'.
findings.remediation: C-13: exit only when payload.action ~= 'renamed'. Add a case in tests/test_drilldown.lua. Smoke test SM-10.

verification.reason: DrillDown:OnWindowsChanged (modules/DrillDown.lua:850-855) exits any view whose id matches payload.windowId, whatever the action. WindowManager:Rename announces (cfg.id, 'renamed') at :316, so renaming a drilled window closes its drill-down even though its data and columns have not changed. Excluding 'renamed' is correct. 'copied' (:499) can change the target's columns, so exiting on it should stay.

findings.title: UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED and CHAT_MSG_SYSTEM stay registered all session for narrow uses, and neither is measured
findings.evidence: No perf bucket brackets either handler, so their cost is unverified.
findings.remediation: C-15, measurement only: add the handlers to an existing bucket or a debug-only counter. A new bucket needs its descriptor entry in core/PerfSetup.lua and its bracket in the same commit. Decide on registration changes next cycle from the numbers.

verification.reason: core/MultiMeters.lua:201 and :208 register both events in OnEnable for the whole session. The comment at :196-199 calls UNIT_SPELLCAST_SUCCEEDED 'the busiest thing this addon listens to'. core/PerfSetup.lua:103-122 declares no bucket covering OnSpellSucceeded or OnSystemMessage, and only the DAMAGE_METER handlers (:419-432) carry a Perf bracket. performance-§3 says hot-path handlers SHOULD be bracketed and that every declared bucket must be reached, which matches the remediation (declare the bucket and add its bracket in the same commit). Both handlers return early, so the impact is unmeasured cost, not a known cost. Low and measurement-only is right.

findings.title: 28 LibKa0s tags (v1.18.0 to v1.53.0) were vendored with no re-vendor bundle and no register row
findings.evidence: The commits name 34 distinct tags since the 2026-08-25 horizon. The bundles name 8 tags (v1.15.0, v1.25.0, v1.30.0, v1.31.0-v1.34.0, v1.55.0). The kit-only v1.54.2 (d2169d4) is not seen by the check. The High comes from AUDIT.md step 4; by player impact this would be Low.
findings.remediation: Write one consolidated bundle, docs/revendor/<date>-v1.34.0-to-v1.54.2/ (or widen it to v1.15.0 -> v1.54.2, or add a second bundle for v1.15.0 -> v1.30.0). Its 01_DELTA.md first line names the span, and 05_SUMMARY.md records the carrying commit and any adoption per tag. Do not back-fill a folder per tag. Any later collection re-vendor writes its own bundle.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (A re-vendor commit implies a bundle); AUDIT.md step 4

verification.reason: I read the CLAUDE.md provenance line at each of the 39 commits since 2026-08-25 that touch libs/LibKa0s. Together they vendor 34 distinct tags, v1.18.0 through v1.55.0. The docs/revendor bundles, read from their folder names and 01_DELTA.md first lines, record v1.15.0, v1.25.0, v1.30.0, v1.31.0-v1.34.0 and v1.55.0. That leaves 28 tags unrecorded, matching the finding. ARCHITECTURE.md has no deviation row. audit-review-history ('A re-vendor commit implies a bundle') is a MUST, AUDIT.md:341-347 sets it at High, and the same rule says one consolidated bundle naming the span discharges the backlog, which is what the remediation proposes. The severity follows the playbook, and the evidence already notes that player impact is low.

findings.title: Event registration is not isolated per event, and rejected names are not recorded
findings.evidence: There are 21 bare self:RegisterEvent calls, so the first unknown name aborts every later one, including DAMAGE_METER_*. registerIfValid calls RegisterEvent outside the pcall. The :153-156 comment wrongly says an unknown event costs nothing. Nothing reachable by the player records rejections.
findings.remediation: Add a single pcall-wrapped registerEvent(target, event, handler) with IsEventValid as a front gate, and route all 22 registrations through a module-level EVENTS list. Keep failures in NS.State.rejectedEvents, reset on each OnEnable, with a debug line. Show them in /mm debug diag. Add a test_lifecycle case using M.__badEvents. Fix the comment and add a note in docs/midnight-quirks.md. Keep target=self so Disabled 3 and Disabled 9 stay green.

verification.reason: I counted 21 bare self:RegisterEvent calls in core/MultiMeters.lua:134-215. registerIfValid (:124-132) calls target:RegisterEvent outside the pcall once IsEventValid passes. The :153-156 comment claims an unregistered-namespace event 'costs nothing', which is wrong, because an unknown name raises. Nothing in core, modules or tests references rejectedEvents or __badEvents. events-frames-taint-§1 ('An unknown event name raises...') has three MUSTs: per-event pcall isolation, recording the rejected names, and making that record reachable by the player. The kit mock supports M.__badEvents (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725), and Disabled 3 and Disabled 9 exist in tests/test_disabled.lua:166 and :456, so the remediation is sound. On the current client every name is valid, so Low fits the reachable impact.

findings.title: Tag 1.0.1-release ships a TOC saying 1.0.0, with no Version History row and no release run

Roll Version History, optionally with a '1.0.1 re-published 1.0.0 unchanged' row. Run the release battery with all four suites at pass before tagging. Never cut a tag without the bump.

README.md:101-104 has no 1.0.1 row, and the manifest.json release values are 0.1.0 x2, 1.0.0 x1 and null x6, with no 1.0.1. versioning-git:6 requires the version to be bumped in the TOC and in the Version History. findings.title: British 'minimise'/'minimised' survives in player-visible strings, README, identifiers and comments, held by an unsanctioned waiver
findings.locations: locales/enUS.lua:214; locales/enUS.lua:231; README.md:50; modules/HeaderControls.lua:127; tests/prose_waivers.lua:24; tests/prose_waivers.lua:30-57

findings.title: A disabled addon still draws, outlines and arms drag on every unlocked panel: Unlock:Decorate overrides the stand-down latch
findings.locations: modules/Canvas.lua:802, modules/Canvas.lua:823, modules/Unlock.lua:171-177, modules/Unlock.lua:123-126, settings/Schema.lua:503-509, settings/Slash.lua:342, settings/PanelEditor.lua:749-750
findings.evidence: Canvas:Render sets spec.shown=false when NS.Lifecycle:IsDown() (:802), then calls NS.Unlock:Decorate(f, rec) (:823). Decorate runs f:Show() and ArmDrag (EnableMouse, SetMovable, RegisterForDrag) and never consults the latch. A headless probe on the real TOC with two panels gave: unlocked then disabled, shown=2; disabled plus per-panel unlock, shown=1; disabled plus Lock frame unticked, shown=2; relocked, shown=0. Three routes reach it: (A) unlock then disable; (B) the Lock frame row or /pm set state.locked false while disabled; (C) the per-panel Unlock tick while disabled. Dragging a panel then writes db.profile.panels while the addon is off.
findings.remediation: In Canvas:Render, read the latch once (local down = NS.Lifecycle and NS.Lifecycle:IsDown()). If down, call NS.Unlock:StripOverlay(f); otherwise call NS.Unlock:Decorate(f, rec). Keep the session unlock state (NS.State.unlocked, unlockedPanels) untouched so NS.StandUp -> RenderAll restores the outlines from current state (performance-§6). Rejected alternatives: an imperative Hide or force-lock sweep in NS.StandDown (anti-pattern #85), and per-surface disabled gates. Land it test-first with R-02. Add an unlock-then-disable case to docs/smoke-tests.md.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (every frame hidden, enforced at the source); performance-§6; anti-pattern #85

verification.reason: modules/Canvas.lua:802 sets spec.shown=false under NS.Lifecycle:IsDown(), then :823 calls NS.Unlock:Decorate unconditionally. modules/Unlock.lua:171-177 (Decorate) checks only IsPanelUnlocked, then runs f:Show() and ArmDrag (EnableMouse/SetMovable/RegisterForDrag). The latch is never consulted. NS.StandDown (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:93-95) only calls RenderAll, so an unlocked panel stays drawn and draggable. The schema Lock row (settings/Schema.lua:503-509) and the per-panel tick (PanelEditor.lua:749-750) reach SetUnlocked/SetPanelUnlocked without a disabled check. That breaks slash-commands-§7 ('The disabled state is total (MUST)'). Remediation is correct: branch on the latch in Render and call StripOverlay, keeping session state so StandUp -> RenderAll restores it. It adds no new deviation. Severity high holds because a MUST is broken on a common path, and drags write the DB while the addon is off.

findings.title: 'Only in combat' and 'Only out of combat' visibility never flip at combat start because Compat.InCombat uses InCombatLockdown
findings.evidence: Compat.InCombat() returns InCombatLockdown(). Lockdown begins after PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED and ends before PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED, so it reads false inside both handlers. OnRegenDisabled -> RenderForCombat() therefore rebuilds every spec with inCombat=false. An inCombat profile stays hidden for the whole fight and an outOfCombat profile stays visible. events-frames-taint-§2 names this exact shape.
findings.remediation: Thread the transition's truth from the event: OnRegenDisabled -> NS.Canvas:RenderForCombat(true), and OnRegenEnabled -> RenderForCombat(false) after ResumePending. Add an optional inCombat parameter to Canvas:Render, RenderAll and RenderForCombat (Render defaults it to NS.Compat.InCombat()). Change Compat.InCombat() to prefer UnitAffectingCombat('player'), presence-guarded, with InCombatLockdown as the fallback. Add UnitAffectingCombat to .luacheckrc read_globals. Keep the unlock deferral on InCombatLockdown. Keep BuildSpec pure. Verify in-client (smoke C-03).

verification.reason: core/Compat.lua:79-82 returns InCombatLockdown(). modules/Canvas.lua:787 feeds it to BuildSpec. core/PanelMaster.lua:116-127 has OnRegenDisabled -> RenderForCombat() -> RenderAll with no combat truth threaded through. At PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED lockdown has not begun, so the render uses inCombat=false and the 'inCombat'/'outOfCombat' modes do not flip at combat start. A caveat on the evidence: at REGEN_ENABLED the false reading is the CORRECT answer, so only the combat-start transition is broken. The stated impact (hidden or visible for the whole fight) is still accurate. events-frames-taint-§2 (STANDARDS.md v1.8.0 changelog, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1267) says combat-reactive display SHOULD use UnitAffectingCombat and transitions SHOULD ride the REGEN events, which matches the finding. The remediation keeps the unlock deferral on InCombatLockdown, as the standard requires.

findings.locations: modules/Registry.lua:876-904, modules/Registry.lua:892-895, modules/Canvas.lua:566-569, modules/Canvas.lua:112-113, modules/Canvas.lua:85-89, modules/Unlock.lua:211

findings.title: A profile switch that swaps which id owns which frame name creates a duplicate named frame and orphans one each switch
findings.evidence: RenderAll resolves mismatches one id at a time. When id 1 wants a name still held by active[2], acquire runs CreateFrame with that global name a second time. When id 2 is released, its frame overwrites the pool slot, and the earlier frame becomes unreachable. A probe alternating {1 Alpha, 2 Xray}/{1 Xray, 2 Alpha} six times recorded 6 named CreateFrame calls, with PooledCount stuck at 1. test_profiles.lua never swaps ids.
findings.remediation: Make Canvas:RenderAll(inCombat) two-pass. First build want[id]=Registry.FrameName(rec), then release every active frame that is retired or whose __frameName is not want[id], then Render each id. Keep the Render(id) single-id mismatch branch as the fallback. Add a test_profiles case, red first, that swaps names across ids several times through OnProfileChanged and asserts zero named CreateFrame calls after the first render, plus _G-name/active identity.

verification.reason: acquire (modules/Canvas.lua:36-40, pool keyed by global name) and the per-id mismatch branch in Render (:811-820), driven one id at a time by RenderAll (:829-842), show the problem. When id1 wants the name still held by active[id2], pool[name] is empty and newFrame creates a second frame with the same global name. A later release overwrites pool[name] and orphans a frame on each alternating switch. WoW frames are never collected, so this is a permanent leak, and _G[name] can point at a different frame than the active one. The pool's own comment (:25-40) claims the bound is one frame per name, which this breaks. The two-pass RenderAll remediation is sound and keeps the single-id fallback.

findings.title: The per-panel Unlock tick on the Panels page can show a state the panel is not in
findings.evidence: The tick has no refresher. It reads IsPanelUnlocked, which is true whenever the global unlock is on, so unticking it while globally unlocked has no effect. findings.remediation: Give the tick a scalar refresher that reads NS.Unlock:IsPanelUnlocked(rec.id). Disable it, with a tooltip line, while the global unlock is on. From the end of U:SetUnlocked, U:SetPanelUnlocked and U:ResumePending, call NS.PanelEditor:RefreshUnlock() behind a presence guard (precedent: modules/Registry.lua:516). Do not add a new bus message. PanelEditor.lua is 1476 lines, so keep the change to 12 added lines or fewer, or land it after the issue #47 split; it must never cross 1500.

verification.reason: settings/PanelEditor.lua:743-758 has no refresher (the comment says so). It reads IsPanelUnlocked, which returns true when NS.State.unlocked (modules/Unlock.lua:123-126), so unticking while globally unlocked does nothing visible. A global lock clears unlockedPanels without refreshing the editor. On deferral the box is forced unticked, and U:ResumePending (:271+) later unlocks the panel without refreshing it. findings.title: A profile switch, copy or reset leaves elements placed by the OLD profile, because Anchor reads the features' cached cfg upvalues in an undefined bus dispatch order
findings.locations: modules/Anchor.lua:359; modules/Anchor.lua:123-124 (wrong comment); modules/CastBars.lua:372,408; modules/TargetFrames.lua:258,297; modules/PetFrames.lua:139,178; tests/test_anchor.lua:181-182 (wrong comment); libs/CallbackHandler-1.0/CallbackHandler-1.0.lua:16
findings.evidence: CallbackHandler dispatches with next(), so the order of PROFILE handlers is hash order, not TOC order. spec.config returns a captured cfg upvalue that each feature rebinds only in its own PROFILE handler. Nothing re-anchors afterwards. Reproduced in a scratch script: 'back to Default pet anchoredToHolder=true cfgMode=attached' and 'after Reset all settings target anchoredToHolder=true cfgMode=attached'. The comments at Anchor.lua:123-124 and test_anchor.lua:181-182 wrongly assume registration order equals dispatch order.
findings.remediation: C-001 / T-1: change spec.config to read live data (`function() return NS.db.profile.castbar|target|pet end`) in all three features, and switch the slotSize closures to the same live read. Rewrite the Anchor comment to say CallbackHandler order is undefined. Add real-switch tests to tests/test_anchor.lua (or a new tests/test_profile_switch.lua): SetProfile between profiles that differ in anchorMode, assert __aTarget, repeat after RestoreAllDefaults. Mark the case with `-- red under: revert config() to the captured upvalue`. Rejected: deferring to the next frame, or a second ordered PROFILE message.

verification.reason: Anchor.lua:359 re-applies on MSG.PROFILE through spec.config(), which is `function() return cfg end` over an upvalue rebound only in each feature's own PROFILE handler (CastBars.lua:372/406-408, TargetFrames.lua:258/296-298, PetFrames.lua:139/177-179). CallbackHandler Dispatch (CallbackHandler-1.0.lua:16-22) walks handlers with next() over a table keyed by target, and every receiver has its own NS.NewBusTarget() table, so dispatch order is hash order, not TOC order. The feature handlers' reconfigure/reskin/refresh never call Anchor.Apply, and Providers' PROFILE burst sends LAYOUT only when the frame map changed (Providers.lua:230-237), so nothing re-anchors afterwards. The comments at Anchor.lua:119-126 and test_anchor.lua:178-183 do assume registration order equals dispatch order. The remediation (a live NS.db.profile read in config and slotSize, keeping the shipped-default fallback in placementOf) is sound. High stands: placement stays wrong after a routine profile switch, copy or reset until a reload or an unrelated LAYOUT/CONFIG.

The case meets the Critical floor; the review graded it High because it needs a name collision, and triage may raise it.

Add a test in tests/test_slash.lua (`-- red under: drop the exists() guard in new`). Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit.

verification.reason: Slash.lua:270-274: `new` calls db:SetProfile(name) and then NS.ResetProfileCounted(db) with no existence check, so an existing profile is switched to, wiped and reported as 'Created'. That is silent loss of a whole profile's data from one ordinary command. The rule refs exist (slash-commands §3/§4, localization §1/§5). The remediation (an exists() guard via db:GetProfiles(), a localized refusal and a red-under test) is correct.

findings.title: The stand-down leaves the EditMode.Exit EventRegistry callback registered, and burst() keeps arming two C_Timer.After timers while the addon is disabled
findings.evidence: `pcall(EventRegistry.RegisterCallback, EventRegistry, "EditMode.Exit", burst, Providers)` is registered once in OnEnable. Suspend runs only ev:UnregisterAllEvents(). burst() bumps burstGen and arms two C_Timer.After calls even while suspended. The callback has a real unregister, so the hooksecurefunc carve-out does not apply. The audit graded this Medium (MUST).
findings.remediation: C-004 / T-4 / audit Sprint 1.4: add a registerEditMode(on) or registerCallbacks()/unregisterCallbacks() pair behind the presence guard and pcall. Call it from OnEnable/Resume, and call the unregister from Suspend. burst() returns before it touches burstGen or timers while suspended. Add `-- red under: drop unregisterCallbacks() from Providers:Suspend` / `-- red under: drop the suspended guard in burst`. Rejected: an addon-side tracked-callback helper, which would be a second stand-down record (anti-pattern #85). If one is wanted, it belongs as a LibKa0s Bus minor.

verification.reason: Real as stated. Providers.lua:341-344 registers the EventRegistry 'EditMode.Exit' callback once, in OnEnable. Suspend (348-353) only runs ev:UnregisterAllEvents(), and burst() (61-67) arms two C_Timer.After timers with no suspended check. slash-commands §7 says the hooksecurefunc carve-out MUST NOT be generalized to anything that has a real unregister. Severity is lowered because of what can actually be reached. The PROFILE message path is stood down by the bus record, so the only live trigger is leaving Edit Mode while disabled. Each trigger arms two one-shot timers that end in Providers.Request(), which returns at once because `suspended` is set (line 54). No drawing, no SV write, and the cost is negligible. It is a conformance gap, not user-visible harm. The remediation is otherwise correct: use EventRegistry:UnregisterCallback('EditMode.Exit', Providers) in Suspend and re-register in Resume, both behind the existing presence guard and pcall, and have burst() return early while suspended.

findings.title: The secure-write memo compares against the APPLIED value, so a change reverted in combat is lost (Click to target stays off after combat)
findings.evidence: `if btn.__clicks == on then return end` and `if btn.__driver == driver then return end` are set only inside the deferred closure. Toggling A→B→A in combat therefore leaves B queued. Reproduced: 'setting true btn.__clicks false attr *type1 nil' after leaving combat.
findings.remediation: C-003 / T-3: keep request-side memos (__clicksWant, __driverWant) that are set at request time and used for the early return. __clicks/__driver stay as the applied state inside the closure. Test in tests/test_targetframes.lua (and petframes): force InCombatLockdown, toggle clickToTarget false then true, call OnLeaveCombat, and assert *type1 == 'target'. Mark it `-- red under: compare against btn.__clicks`.

verification.reason: UnitButtons.lua:52-68: ApplyDriver and ApplyClicks early-return on btn.__driver/__clicks, which are set only inside the deferred RunSecure closure. NS.RunSecure (core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:62-72) queues the latest write per key in combat. So applied=true, then toggle false (queued), then toggle true returns early because __clicks is still true, and the queued false is flushed on PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED. The setting reads on while the button is click-dead, which is reachable in normal play. The request-side memo remediation is correct. Clearing or overwriting the pending key on the early-return path would be an equivalent fix.

findings.title: The stand-down replaces the target and pet buttons' secure state drivers with 'hide' instead of unregistering them
findings.evidence: Driver returns 'hide' when not allowed, and ApplyDriver re-registers it, so ten state drivers stay registered while the addon is disabled. UnregisterStateDriver is declared in .luacheckrc but never called. slash-commands-§7 requires state drivers to be stood down where they can be, which is out of combat.
findings.remediation: C-005 / T-5, after T-3 and T-1: while suspended, refresh calls UnitButtons.Release(btn). Through NS.RunSecure('driver:'..key) it runs UnregisterStateDriver(btn,'visibility'), btn:Hide() and clears __driver, and it sets __driverWant=nil at request time. Stand-up re-registers through refresh. Add tests in tests/test_disabled.lua: no __drivers.visibility after an out-of-combat disable, re-enable restores the driver, and the in-combat variant completes after OnLeaveCombat. Mark them `-- red under: keep the "hide" driver`. Needs a combat smoke test (S-005).

verification.reason: Real. TargetFrames.lua:185-188 (and the PetFrames equivalent) compute allowed=false while suspended, and UnitButtons.Driver returns 'hide', which ApplyDriver registers with RegisterStateDriver. The ten state drivers therefore stay registered while the addon is disabled, and UnregisterStateDriver is never called anywhere (only declared at .luacheckrc:31). slash-commands §7 explicitly says secure state drivers are stood down where they can be, and deferred out of combat. Severity is lowered for impact: a constant 'hide' driver only costs the secure state-driver manager's periodic evaluation of ten trivial conditions. Nothing is drawn or written and the player sees nothing. It is a MUST conformance gap with negligible reachable cost. The remediation (a Release through NS.RunSecure that unregisters, hides, clears __driver and resets the request memo from R-04) is correct. Its ordering after R-04 is right because it depends on the __driverWant memo.

findings.title: The zero-overhead perf scenario compares capture-off with capture-on instead of with instrumentation absent
findings.evidence: `assert_(probeOff.bytesPerIter <= probeOn.bytesPerIter + 1, ...)` would pass a dormant bracket that allocates as much as an armed one. The probeOverheadOff ≤ 24 B ceiling only partly compensates. Today: off 0.0 B/iter, on 0.5 B/iter.
findings.remediation: C-007 / T-6: preferred is a second environment where NS.Perf is pre-seeded with a constant-false `on`. The practical alternative wraps debugprofilestop and NS.Perf.Note with counters and asserts 0 calls per iteration while Perf.on==false, plus asserts probeOff.bytesPerIter <= castStartStop.bytesPerIter + 1. Comment on why this stands in for 'absent'. Add no wall-clock assertion. It stays a scenario and does not go in docs/test-cases.md.

verification.reason: Real. tests/perf.lua:234-240 compares capture-off with capture-on, but performance §9 requires the zero-overhead scenario to pin capture-off against the same path 'with the instrumentation absent'. Severity is lowered: tests/perf.lua is a measurement runner outside the green gate (testing §7). Today's figures show off=0.0 B/iter, and the 24 B probeOverheadOff ceiling already bounds it, so this is missing evidence rather than a shipped regression. The remediation's 'practical alternative' is also flawed. `probeOff.bytesPerIter <= castStartStop.bytesPerIter + 1` compares capture-off against another capture-off measurement (Perf.on is false at perf.lua:173). castStartStop also runs FIVE start/stop cycles per iteration against castOnce's one, and measures 16.6 B/iter, so the bound is about 16 B looser than intended and not an 'absent' baseline at all.
verification.corrected_remediation: Build a true 'absent' baseline and do not compare against castStartStop. Preferred: load a second environment where NS.Perf is pre-seeded so the bracket compiles to nothing, or where the bracket helpers are stubbed out, then measure castOnce there and assert probeOff.bytesPerIter <= absent.bytesPerIter + 1. Acceptable fallback: wrap debugprofilestop and NS.Perf.Note with call counters, assert 0 calls per iteration while Perf.on == false, and keep the existing ceiling. Add a comment explaining why this stands in for 'absent'. Add no wall-clock assertion. It stays a scenario outside docs/test-cases.md.

findings.title: The test kit has no EventRegistry fake or recorder, so test_disabled cannot see the EditMode.Exit survivor

verification.reason: A grep for EventRegistry across tests/ (kit and wow_mock.lua) returns nothing. modules/Providers.lua:342-345 registers EditMode.Exit only when the EventRegistry global exists, so the harness never records it. findings.title: The library-absent Slash stub hand-copies LibKa0s's refusal-line format and row shape, and re-implements its dispatcher; slash-commands-§1 and §7 pull in opposite directions
findings.evidence: `local DISABLED_LINE = "%s is disabled \226\128\148 enable it with |cFFFFFF00%s|r"` copies lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT, and FormatRow copies `cmd — desc`. §1 says a stub MUST NOT re-implement the library's rendering, while §7 requires one collection-wide refusal line even in a degraded build. The parity test pins the drift. The review graded this Low; the audit filed it as Info because it is a question of how two rules interact.
findings.remediation: Upstream first: LibKa0s U-3 (optional) documents the prescribed library-absent Slash stub shape in docs/api Slash 'Degradation', or exports the format as data. WowAddonStandards rules on the §1/§7 interaction, either naming the exception in slash-commands-§1 or requiring the export. Addon C-009 / T-14: keep the stub's dispatch, drop the copied color format, and render a plain '<brand> is disabled; /pfe enable turns it back on (LibKa0s missing)'. Relax test_surface_parity to assert one line naming /pfe enable in both arms. Follow the upstream shape if it lands first.

verification.reason: The evidence is accurate. settings/Slash.lua:327 copies the row formatter (`cmd .. ' — ' .. desc`). :331 copies lib.DISABLED_LINE_FORMAT verbatim (libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:83). The comment at :322-324 ('No formatter ... is copied here') is false. slash-commands-§1 (lines 18-19) forbids a stub from copying the row formatter, but it also requires a stub carrying OnSlash, so a minimal stub dispatch is sanctioned rather than a hand-rolled dispatcher. §7's refusal-line rule (line 81) says the wording 'MUST NOT be re-spelled per addon'. The addon-side remediation, printing a plain '<brand> is disabled; /pfe enable turns it back on (LibKa0s missing)', is itself a per-addon re-spelling of the refusal line, so it would trade one §1/§7 deviation for a §7 deviation. The path is reachable only in a build missing LibKa0s, so Low stands.
verification.corrected_remediation: Upstream first. WowAddonStandards rules on the §1/§7 interaction: either slash-commands-§1 names the refusal line as the one string a library-absent stub may carry, or the rule requires LibKa0s to export the refusal shape as data that a host can bundle. LibKa0s documents the prescribed stub shape in its Slash docs 'Degradation' section. Addon side: now, drop the copied FormatRow em-dash formatter in favour of a plainly rendered row, and correct the false comment at settings/Slash.lua:322-324. Leave the DisabledLine wording alone until the standard rules, then adopt exactly what it prescribes. Do not invent a new per-addon refusal sentence. Adjust test_surface_parity to match the ruled shape.

findings.title: The migration runner migrates only the active profile but stamps the account-wide schemaVersion
findings.evidence: `step.apply(NS.db.profile)` followed by `g.schemaVersion = step.to`. The first real ladder step would leave every non-active profile unmigrated forever. SCHEMA_STEPS is empty today, so nothing can reach it. Review graded Low; audit filed Info (an observation).
findings.remediation: Review C-008 / T-10 (fix now): apply each step to every stored profile (`for name,p in pairs(NS.db.profiles or {[cur]=NS.db.profile})`), with defaults-merge caveats commented, and stamp the global version only after all profiles. Add a unit case with a test-local injected fake step using two profiles. The audit's alternative is to defer until the first step is written, or to migrate lazily on OnProfileChanged with a per-profile stamp.

verification.reason: core/Database.lua:37-48 runs step.apply(NS.db.profile), the active profile only, then stamps the account-wide g.schemaVersion = step.to. The first real step would leave inactive profiles unmigrated for good. SCHEMA_STEPS (:34) is empty, so nothing reaches this today. savedvariables-§1 requires the runner but does not spell out per-profile iteration, so this is a latent correctness trap rather than a standards breach. Low or Info are both defensible, and I keep Low. The remediation is sound, and its fallback handles the non-AceDB path (:25-26 builds NS.db without profiles). The unit case needs a test seam to inject a step, because SCHEMA_STEPS is a file-local.

findings.title: Movable named holder and stand-in frames are not excluded from the client's layout cache
findings.evidence: StartMoving marks a frame as user-placed, so the client persists its position in layout-local.txt beside the addon's own stored position. After Reset position, the two can disagree. Not verified in the client.
findings.remediation: C-008 / T-11, after T-1: presence-guarded `if frame.SetDontSavePosition then frame:SetDontSavePosition(true) end` after Anchor.lua:257 and StandIn.lua:153. Verify with smoke S-008: after reset and /reload the frame is at the default spot, and layout-local.txt has no holder entry.

verification.reason: It is true that the holder (modules/Anchor.lua:231, named, SetMovable at :257, StartMoving at :261/:271) and the stand-in (modules/StandIn.lua:152-158, named, StartMoving) never call SetDontSavePosition, so the client may cache them in layout-local.txt. The reachable impact is essentially nil. Both frames are re-anchored explicitly by the addon from its own stored or default position: holder:ClearAllPoints/SetPoint at Anchor.lua:101-102, and f:ClearAllPoints plus SetPoint at the stored or center position around StandIn.lua:198-206. Any cached client position is overwritten when the addon applies its layout. The finding itself says it is not verified in the client, and the 'compat' rule_ref names no clause that requires SetDontSavePosition (a grep of the standard finds no mention). This is hygiene, so Info, not Low.
verification.corrected_remediation: Optional hygiene (C-008 / T-11): add a presence-guarded `if frame.SetDontSavePosition then frame:SetDontSavePosition(true) end` after holder:SetMovable (Anchor.lua:257) and f:SetMovable (StandIn.lua:153), so the client stops writing cache entries the addon always overrides. Verify in-game only by checking layout-local.txt, since the visible position is already the addon's. Cite no standards clause, because none requires it.

findings.title: Session-long event registrations bypass the per-feature syncEvents discipline, and debug arguments are built even with debug off
findings.evidence: PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and RAID_TARGET_UPDATE are registered at file load for every enabled session, including solo and feature-off. Preview's PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED stays registered while not previewing. UnitName(...) is called just to build an NS.Debug argument on every UNIT_TARGET/UNIT_PET, even with debug off.
findings.remediation: C-008 / T-12, after T-1 and T-5: guard the NS.Debug argument construction with `if NS.State.debug`. Move PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and RAID_TARGET_UPDATE into each module's syncEvents (feature on and in a party). Move Preview's PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED into listen(on). Re-run test_disabled and confirm R_on is still non-empty.

verification.reason: modules/TargetFrames.lua:320 and :326 register PLAYER_TARGET_CHANGED and RAID_TARGET_UPDATE on the module's bus target at file load, outside syncEvents (:208). Preview.lua:154 registers PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED unconditionally, while listen(on) at :79 gates only GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE. TargetFrames.lua:205 and PetFrames.lua:83 evaluate UnitName(btn.token) as an NS.Debug argument on every event, with debug on or off. When the whole addon is disabled the bus unregisters, so the cost is limited to the feature-off, solo and not-previewing cases, where handlers early-return. That is a small dispatch cost, so low is right. The rule_ref is loose: events-frames-taint-§1 is not a dispatch-cost rule, and the performance section would be a better citation. The remediation is sound.

findings.title: Event registrations are bare loops with no per-event pcall, no C_EventUtils.IsEventValid gate and no record of rejected names
findings.locations: core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:140; modules/CastBars.lua:336; modules/Providers.lua:330-336; modules/PetFrames.lua:103-107; modules/TargetFrames.lua:214,320,326; modules/RangeFade.lua:168; modules/Preview.lua:81,154
findings.evidence: `for event, method in pairs(LIFECYCLE_EVENTS) do self:RegisterEvent(event, method) end` and `for i = 1, #EVENTS do el:RegisterUnitEvent(EVENTS[i], unit) end`. `grep IsEventValid` finds nothing. One retired event name would leave every later event in the block unregistered. This is latent: every name is valid on 12.1.0. Two MUSTs and one SHOULD fail.
findings.remediation: Audit Sprint 1.1-1.2: add NS.SafeRegister(target, event, handler, unit) in core/, gated by C_EventUtils.IsEventValid, pcall per event, with rejects recorded in NS.RejectedEvents. Route every site through it. Surface NS.RejectedEvents in /pfe status (only when non-empty) and in the DebugLog initSummary. Write the test first with M.__badEvents naming one cast event, and assert the other 12 still register. Record the trade-off in docs/midnight-quirks.md and the status row in docs/slash-dispatch.md.

verification.reason: This is real. core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:140 is a bare pairs loop over RegisterEvent, CastBars.lua:336 is a bare RegisterUnitEvent loop, and there is no IsEventValid, pcall or rejected-name record anywhere outside libs/. events-frames-taint.md:30-31 sets two MUSTs: survive one bad name through a pcalled helper, and record the rejects where the player can reach them. The evidence overstates one point. The IsEventValid bullet (:32) is a SHOULD only for 'a name newer than the clients it supports', and every name here is long-established, so that SHOULD does not currently bind. Two MUSTs fail, not two MUSTs and one SHOULD. The gate is still a reasonable addition. The kit already supports the proposed test: LibKa0s testkit mock_base.lua:715-727 implements M.__badEvents. LibKa0s has no shared SafeRegister helper, so a local core/ helper is the right routing.
verification.corrected_remediation: Add NS.SafeRegister in core/: one pcall per event, rejected names recorded in NS.RejectedEvents, and IsEventValid as an optional front gate that is never the only guard. Route every RegisterEvent and RegisterUnitEvent site through it. Make NS.RejectedEvents reachable through the reserved debug verb or the debug console, as §1 requires; /pfe status can also show it. Write the test first using the kit's existing M.__badEvents. Record the probing trade-off in the quirks doc. Optionally raise upstream whether LibKa0s should ship this helper, since five repos have each written their own.
