findings.title: PrettyChat rewrites CHAT_MSG_LOOT/CURRENCY text at runtime; LootHistory compiles its loot/currency patterns once and silently stops recording
findings.locations: modules/Override.lua:292, modules/Override.lua:302, modules/Override.lua:121-127, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:151, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:118, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:147, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:187, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:210
findings.evidence: ApplyStrings sets _G[globalName] on every settings write, latch transition, profile event and, while the combat watcher is armed, every combat boundary (visibility inCombat/outOfCombat). LootHistory caches lootPatterns/currencyPatterns on first parse (`local pats = lootPatterns or Util.BuildLootPatterns()`) and never rebuilds them. After any change, self-loot and self-currency in the other state go unrecorded, with no error. The mechanism is inferred from PrettyChat's own premise and is unverified in-client. findings.remediation: PrettyChat side (C-01): add a Known Limitations bullet in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md saying PrettyChat rewrites the CHAT_MSG_LOOT/CURRENCY/MONEY/COMBAT_* payload for every addon, that parsers must build patterns from the live global or revalidate them, and that inCombat/outOfCombat modes change these globals at every combat boundary. Name handoff H-1. Add one sentence to docs/scope.md and add SMK-F001 to docs/smoke-tests.md. Cross-repo (H-1, LootHistory): Util.ParseSelfLoot (:145) and ParseSelfCurrency (:208) record the source global values the cache was built from and rebuild when any differs (about 10 string-identity compares per line). Add a LootHistory test that flips a global between two parses. File a LootHistory issue citing F-001. Do not add a PrettyChat public API, bus message or chat filter. Verify in-client with SMK-F001 (/etrace arg1 changes with combat state).

verification.upstream_repo: LootHistory (cross-repo handoff H-1; not a library/standards change)
verification.reason: Mechanism is real: Override.lua:292 writes _G[globalName] on every ApplyStrings pass, and the combat watcher (Override.lua:121-127, PLAYER_REGEN_* at :138) re-runs it at each combat boundary when visibility is inCombat or outOfCombat. LootHistory/core/Util.lua:118/147 and :187/210 cache lootPatterns/currencyPatterns once and never rebuild them. Severity is lowered because the default visibility is 'always' (settings/Schema.lua:120). Under defaults, LootHistory usually builds its patterns lazily after PrettyChat has applied, so it breaks only after a mid-session string edit, toggle, profile change or perf stand-down. Constant breakage needs the opt-in combat modes, and the finding is still unverified in-client. That is silent data loss in a sibling addon, but only on non-default or mid-session paths, so medium rather than high. The remediation and routing (fix the consumer in LootHistory, document it in PrettyChat, add no new API) are sound.

findings.title: Migration runner migrates only the active profile (global stamp) and stamps past a step that raised
findings.evidence: `local from = db.global.schemaVersion or 0`, and schemaVersion is stamped unconditionally after runSteps. A failed step is printed and counted as ran. There is no impact today because the migrations table is empty, but F-002's fix writes the first migration.

Split the steps into profileSteps (idempotent, shape-detecting, run on every load-pass entry regardless of the stamp) and globalSteps (gated by the stamp). runSteps returns false if any step raised, and the stamp moves only when all steps succeed. Rewrite the core/PrettyChat.lua:54-56 comment. Add tests in tests/test_database.lua: a profile step runs on OnProfileChanged into a second profile after the stamp moved, and a raising global step leaves the stamp unmoved (with -- red under: notes). verification.reason: Confirmed in core/Database.lua. :42 has an empty migrations table. runSteps (:85-90) counts a step that raised as ran. findings.title: Categories page Defaults button (and Blizzard footer forward) resets only the selected tab; the rule requires page-wide
findings.evidence: defaultsOnClick calls PrettyChat:ResetCategory(activeCategory(ctx)). The tooltip reads 'Reset the strings on the selected category tab to their defaults.' options-ui-§13: its blast radius MUST NOT narrow to the visible tab. The README documents the narrow behaviour, but there is no register row.
findings.remediation: Owner decision. (a) Make it page-wide per the rule: one Schema.ResetRows batch over all eight categories' rows, one [Set] reset Categories line, a new tooltip key (old key removed), an optional confirmation popup, and README/settings-panel.md/schema.md:158/smoke tests updated in the same commit. Or (b) ratify it with a Documented deviations row keyed options-ui-§13 (trigger: an options-ui revision naming a per-tab reset control, or the category tabs becoming one schema group). Extend the test_panel Defaults case to assert the chosen scope and that the footer OnDefault forwards to it.

verification.reason: settings/Panel.lua:738 sets the tooltip 'Reset the strings on the selected category tab...', and :752-754 has defaultsOnClick call PrettyChat:ResetCategory(activeCategory(ctx)). options-ui.md:316 says: 'The per-page Defaults button stays page-wide ... its blast radius MUST NOT narrow to the visible tab.' README.md:31 and :62 document the per-tab behaviour. The only options-ui-§13 row in ARCHITECTURE.md's Documented deviations (line 274) covers the TreeGroup secondary division, not the Defaults scope. So this is an unratified MUST deviation. Medium is defensible: the narrowing is documented and less destructive, but it breaks a MUST.

findings.title: TOC: load-bearing core\CoreSetup.lua position has no comment
findings.evidence: CoreSetup must follow core\PrettyChat.lua, because NewAddon's AceConsole embed overwrites NS.Print and CoreSetup's last line reclaims it. If it is moved earlier, nothing errors, but every chat line turns green with a trailing colon (anti-pattern #36).
findings.remediation: Add an at-line comment above core\CoreSetup.lua naming what resolves. Comment only, no reordering. Do it in the same edit as PC-78/79/80/60, and align ARCHITECTURE.md:35 and module-map.md load order with the TOC. Optionally add a test_doc_structure case pinning the hub's load-bearing list against the TOC comments.

verification.reason: PrettyChat.toc:52-53 (core\PrettyChat.lua, core\CoreSetup.lua) has no comment on either line. core/PrettyChat.lua:14 calls NewAddon(NS, ..., 'AceConsole-3.0'), which embeds :Print over NS. core/CoreSetup.lua:142 reclaims NS.Print at file scope. Moving CoreSetup earlier would let the embed win silently. toc-file.md:145 requires a load-bearing position to carry an at-line comment naming what resolves. The current ARCHITECTURE.md:33 load-order line also omits core/LifecycleSetup, which the TOC has, so the doc-alignment part of the remediation is warranted.

findings.title: Authored generator GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py is not under tools/
findings.locations: GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py, .pkgmeta:39, DEPENDENCIES.md:146-150, docs/common-tasks.md, docs/global-strings.md, GlobalStrings/README.md, tests/prose_waivers.lua:7, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:270
findings.evidence: layout-§1 (v2.61.0) names this exact file as owing the move. It is not ratified.
findings.remediation: git mv GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py to tools/split_globalstrings.py and keep the chunks where they are. Add '- tools' to .pkgmeta. Update DEPENDENCIES.md, common-tasks.md, global-strings.md, GlobalStrings/README.md, prose_waivers.lua:7, and the layout-§2 register row's Why. Verify that the script's repo-root paths still resolve (it asserts on PrettyChat.toc) and that .pkgmeta checks (a)/(b)/(c) stay clean.

verification.reason: The finding is real. layout.md:93 names GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py as newly non-compliant and owing the move to tools/split_globalstrings.py, and tools/ does not exist yet. The remediation is inaccurate, though. It says to 'verify the repo-root paths still resolve', but they will NOT resolve after a plain git mv. The script derives every path from its own directory: split_globalstrings.py:117-119 sets script_dir, then input_path = script_dir/GlobalStrings.lua and output_dir = script_dir, and :194 reads the TOC at dirname(script_dir). After the move it would look for tools/GlobalStrings.lua, write chunks into tools/, and still find the TOC by luck. The script needs a code change in the same commit.
verification.corrected_remediation: git mv GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py tools/split_globalstrings.py. In the same commit, change main() so that repo_root = dirname(dirname(abspath(__file__))), input_path = repo_root/GlobalStrings/GlobalStrings.lua, output_dir = repo_root/GlobalStrings, and the TOC path is repo_root/PrettyChat.toc. Run it once and confirm that git diff over GlobalStrings/ is empty. Add '- tools' to .pkgmeta ignore. Update the paths in DEPENDENCIES.md, docs/common-tasks.md, docs/global-strings.md, GlobalStrings/README.md, tests/prose_waivers.lua:7, and the regenerate command inside the ARCHITECTURE.md:270 layout-§2 row. Re-check the three conditions of the layout-§1 generated-data exemption (ARCHITECTURE.md 'Files over the 1500-line cap', which ties the dump's exemption to its generator) against the generator's new location.

findings.title: Combat watcher is a private CreateFrame carrying non-unit events; the standard contradicts itself (events-frames-taint-§1 vs library-stack-§1)
findings.evidence: CreateFrame('Frame','PrettyChatCombatWatcher') registers PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/_ENABLED. §1 requires AceEvent, and its carve-out excludes a private RegisterEvent for events the client does not filter by unit. library-stack-§1 cites this very frame as the reason AceEvent is 'when used'. Stand-down is correct, so there is no player impact.
findings.remediation: Upstream first (Sprint 0.1): file a WowAddonStandards issue to widen the §1 carve-out to a lazily-created, fully stood-down boundary-event frame, or to state that such an addon records a row. If the rule is kept, add a Documented deviations row keyed events-frames-taint-§1 (trigger: the first additional event, or a second event-registering module). Vendoring AceEvent is not recommended.

verification.reason: modules/Override.lua:120 CreateFrame('Frame','PrettyChatCombatWatcher') and :138-140 register PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/_ENABLED. events-frames-taint.md:7 MUSTs AceEvent and forbids per-module frames for ordinary event traffic, and :24 says a private RegisterEvent for an event the client does not filter by unit is outside the carve-out. library-stack.md:24 cites this same frame as the reason PrettyChat needs no AceEvent. The register in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:269-277 has no events-frames-taint-§1 row. This is tension between the two sections rather than a literal contradiction, since library-stack only makes AceEvent 'when used'. The addon still deviates from ef-§1 with no row. Stand-down is correct, so low severity holds and routing the fix upstream is right.

findings.title: Event registrations are a bare loop with no pcall helper and no record of rejected names
findings.evidence: `for _, event in ipairs({...}) do combatWatcher:RegisterEvent(event) end`. A retired event name would raise, or silently deafen the watcher, with no record.
findings.remediation: Add a registerEvent(frame, event) helper: C_EventUtils.IsEventValid front gate, pcall(frame.RegisterEvent), and a rejected-name record in NS.RejectedEvents. Surface it in /pc debug and in the [Init] summary. Add a test using the kit's M.__badEvents to prove one bad name leaves the other registered and is recorded. Keep test_disabled green.

verification.reason: modules/Override.lua:138-140 is a bare ipairs loop over combatWatcher:RegisterEvent. events-frames-taint.md:30-33 MUSTs a pcall'ed per-event helper and a player-reachable record of rejected names, and SHOULDs a C_EventUtils.IsEventValid front gate. There is no IsEventValid or RejectedEvents anywhere in core/, modules/ or libs/LibKa0s. The MUST is broken, but both events are long-lived core events, so the reachable impact is low. The remediation matches the rule. The kit mock supports M.__badEvents (ef.md:35).

findings.title: architecture-§4 closed-message-bus MUST binds (a module registers game events), but there is no bus and no register row; the threshold is ambiguous
findings.evidence: The §4 threshold is 'two or more feature modules, or any module that registers game events'. The ## Message Bus section justifies the absence with 'publishes no named message' and a re-check trigger at the first LibStub('AceEvent-3.0'), and neither is the rule's threshold. The clobber hazard cannot arise with one module and one private frame.
findings.remediation: Decide upstream together with PC-84 (Sprint 0.2). If WowAddonStandards narrows the event arm (to modules registering through a shared AceEvent target, or to a second receiver), rewrite the ## Message Bus sentence to cite it. Otherwise add a Documented deviations row keyed architecture-§4 (trigger: a second feature module or a second event-registering module). Do not adopt a bus.

verification.reason: architecture.md:64-65: the MUST binds 'any module that registers game events'. modules/Override.lua:139 registers two events. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:137-145 (## Message Bus) justifies having no bus by 'publishes no named message' and an AceEvent re-check trigger, not by the rule's threshold. There is no architecture-§4 row in the register (lines 269-277). The rationale in architecture.md:68-71 (the same-target clobber) cannot arise with a single private frame, so the impact is nil and low severity holds. It is right to decide this upstream together with A-08.

findings.title: toc-file-§1 register row still records the absent X-Wago-ID as a deviation (it is a MAY)
findings.evidence: The row's What/Why say X-Wago-ID is absent and that toc-file-§1 asks for both distribution ids. Omitting it is compliant, so the Wago half is a graveyard entry.
findings.remediation: Narrow the row to the brand mark: strike the Wago clauses, reduce the trigger to 'a decision to retire the brand mark', and record the narrowing in the retired block. Issue #7 stays will-not-do.

verification.reason: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:271 records '## X-Wago-ID is absent' and says 'toc-file-§1 asks for both distribution ids'. toc-file.md:30 makes X-Wago-ID optional (MAY), included only when the addon is listed on Wago, so omitting it is compliant and the row's claim misstates the rule. The brand-mark half of the row stays valid.

findings.title: The debug-logging-§2 register row records compliant behaviour and should be retired
findings.evidence: The row's own Why says core/MediaSetup.lua calls Media.RegisterLSM like every other addon, which is exactly what debug-logging-§2 asks. The no-op without LSM follows from library-stack-§3.
findings.remediation: Retire the row into the retired block with the date and this reasoning. Optionally keep the fixed-monospace note as prose.

verification.reason: The row at docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:272 says core/MediaSetup.lua calls Media.RegisterLSM(addonName). debug-logging.md §2 asks for exactly that: the path handed over as the descriptor's font, registration via Media.RegisterLSM, and a MAY for pinning the font without a picker. An RegisterLSM that returns 0,0 because LSM is not vendored follows library-stack-§3. The row records compliant behaviour, so retiring it is correct.

findings.title: The vendored automated-test runner cannot record the performance-§12 exemption; RESULTS.md denies an exemption the addon holds
findings.evidence: The runner (kit rev 25) hard-codes a single skip reason ('ships no tests/perf.lua ... rather than a ratified performance-§12 exemption'). automated-tests-§3 requires reason (2), naming performance-§12, when it applies. testing-§1 forbids editing the kit in place.
findings.remediation: Upstream LibKa0s first (Sprint 1.1). testkit/run-automated-tests.sh detects a performance-§12 row under ## Documented deviations in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (or root CLAUDE.md for a library), or accepts an explicit consumer fact (KA0S_PERF_EXEMPT or an opts file). It emits reason (2) in manifest skipReason and in the standing paragraph. Add a kit self-test with two fixtures and a changelog entry. Tag, re-vendor whole, and re-run at the next release. No hand-edits here.

verification.reason: tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh:343-344 sets a single skip note when tests/perf.lua is absent. Lines 838-842 hard-code the 'first reason ... rather than a ratified performance-§12 exemption' paragraph, which docs/automated-tests/RESULTS.md:58-62 reproduces. PrettyChat does hold a performance-§12 row (ARCHITECTURE.md:269). automated-tests.md:126-128 MUSTs recording reason (2), naming performance-§12, when it applies. Upstream LibKa0s testkit/run-automated-tests.sh (v1.55.0) has no exemption detection either, so the fix has to be made upstream and then re-vendored whole. It is a record-accuracy issue with no player impact, so low severity is right.

findings.remediation: Reword to: 'perf is skipped under the ratified performance-§12 no-combat-path exemption (register row in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), which the release notes name.'

verification.reason: docs/testing.md:238-239 reads 'The one narrow exception is `perf` skipped because this addon ships no `tests/perf.lua`, which the release notes state out loud.' automated-tests.md:153-154 says an exempt addon's release notes name the performance-§12 exemption rather than the bare absence, and PrettyChat does hold that exemption (ARCHITECTURE.md:373). findings.title: No core/Compat.lua, and the legacy GetAddOnMetadata is called directly; the standard is inconsistent about whether Compat is required
findings.evidence: compat says every addon MUST ship core/Compat.lua. library-stack-§7 says 'AbsorbTracker and PrettyChat carry none', and the documentation-§3 compat-layer.md trigger counts shims in a possibly-absent file. The legacy call is on the degraded-install path only.
findings.remediation: Upstream first (Sprint 0.3): ask WowAddonStandards whether the MUST binds an addon with zero addon-specific shims. If it does, add a minimal core/Compat.lua (TOC before EnvSetup, annotated) with NS.Compat.GetAddOnMetadata owning the legacy rung, have EnvSetup's fallback call it, and update the compat-layer.md N/A row. If it does not, the finding closes by rule change.

verification.reason: core/ has no Compat.lua. core/EnvSetup.lua:75-76 calls the legacy global GetAddOnMetadata directly on the fallback path, which runs only when the library is absent. compat.md:5 says every addon MUST ship core/Compat.lua, and compat.md:25 says every deprecated-API call MUST route through Compat. library-stack.md:88 says 'AbsorbTracker and PrettyChat carry none', and ARCHITECTURE.md:228 records compat-layer.md as N/A. The standard contradicts itself, so the upstream ruling should come first. The impact is small because the call is on the degraded path only.

findings.title: Defaults hard-coded in multiple places (global defaults in Database.lua; Master-controls defaults typed three times)
findings.evidence: savedvariables-§2 says defaults/Profile.lua MUST be the only place a default is hard-coded. enabled=true and visibility='always' each appear in MASTER_SPEC.defaults, in the reader fallbacks and in the clearing arm.
findings.remediation: Write characterization tests for IsAddonEnabled/GetVisibility first. Add defaults/Global.lua with NS.GlobalDefaults = {schemaVersion=0, minimap={hide=false}}, and assemble Database.defaults at OnInitialize because defaults/ loads after core/. Add NS.GeneralDefaults = {enabled=true, visibility='always'} in defaults/Profile.lua, outside the profile table. Read it from MASTER_SPEC, IsAddonEnabled, GetVisibility and the visibility row's set.

verification.reason: The finding is real. savedvariables.md:33-34 says defaults MUST be declared in defaults/Profile.lua and that it MUST be the only place a default is hardcoded. The code hardcodes them elsewhere: core/Database.lua:34-39 (global schemaVersion and minimap.hide), Override.lua:38 (enabled defaults to true), Override.lua:72-73 ('always' twice), Schema.lua:119-120 (MASTER_SPEC defaults) and Schema.lua:212 (the clearing arm compares against 'always'). The remediation needs one change: the proposed new defaults/Global.lua would itself break §2's 'MUST declare in defaults/Profile.lua'. The global defaults belong in defaults/Profile.lua instead.
verification.corrected_remediation: First write characterization tests for IsAddonEnabled and GetVisibility, plus a test that the global minimap default survives a reset. Declare NS.GlobalDefaults = { schemaVersion = 0, minimap = { hide = false } } and NS.GeneralDefaults = { enabled = true, visibility = 'always' } in defaults/Profile.lua, beside NS.ProfileDefaults. Do not add a new defaults/Global.lua, because savedvariables-§2 names defaults/Profile.lua as the declaration site. defaults/ loads after core/, so assemble Database.defaults.global from NS.GlobalDefaults at OnInitialize. Then read NS.GeneralDefaults from MASTER_SPEC.defaults, IsAddonEnabled, GetVisibility and the General.visibility set arm (Schema.lua:212). The enabled fallback should keep its `== nil` form (savedvariables-§5).

findings.title: settings/Schema.lua publishes NS.Schema non-idempotently
findings.evidence: `local Schema = {}; NS.Schema = Schema`. architecture-§3 requires NS.<Module> = NS.<Module> or {}, and every other module uses that form.
findings.remediation: Change to `NS.Schema = NS.Schema or {}; local Schema = NS.Schema`.

verification.reason: settings/Schema.lua:5-6 is `local Schema = {}` / `NS.Schema = Schema`. architecture.md:57 says modules MUST be published via `NS.<Module> = NS.<Module> or {}`. The finding is accurate, and the remediation is a one-line fix.

findings.title: General subcategory draws no Defaults button; the standard is descriptive rather than explicit
findings.evidence: defaultsButton = false. options-ui-§5's header describes a Defaults button on subcategories, and slash-commands-§2 assumes every schema page has one. The omission is recorded only as a redundancy call, with no register row. Graded as a contract gap, not a MUST.
findings.remediation: Upstream ruling (Sprint 0.6): make the subcategory Defaults button's existence explicit in options-ui-§5. Addon (either way): set defaultsButton = true, add a tooltip L['Reset Enable and General visibility to their defaults.'], and defaultsOnClick = ResetCategory('General'). The allow-list already protects the console and minimap rows (launcher-§3). Update settings-panel.md:79 and extend test_launcher to press the real button. Alternatively, record a register row.

verification.reason: settings/Panel.lua:722 sets defaultsButton = false, and docs/settings-panel.md:79 justifies that only on redundancy grounds. The finding calls the standard descriptive, but it is explicit. options-ui.md:111 gives subcategories a Defaults button, and options-ui.md:114 says the host MUST declare defaultsButton = true with a defaultsTooltip. options-ui.md:260 (§12) says the General page's header Defaults button sits behind the same implementation as Reset all settings and /resetall. That makes this a local deviation that needs no upstream ruling. It also means the proposed defaultsOnClick = ResetCategory('General') is wrong: it would give the General page a Defaults button that does less than Reset all, which §12 forbids.
verification.corrected_remediation: No upstream ruling is needed, because options-ui-§5 (lines 111/114) already requires the button. On the General sub-page, set defaultsButton = true with a defaultsTooltip. Point defaultsOnClick at the same reset-all implementation, with its confirm popup, that the in-body Reset all settings control and /pc resetall use (options-ui-§12, options-ui.md:260), rather than at a General-only ResetCategory. The minimap-hide allow-list must survive that path (launcher-§3), so keep test_launcher asserting it through the real button. Update docs/settings-panel.md:79. The alternative is to keep the omission and record a documented-deviation register row in ARCHITECTURE.md.

findings.title: DEPENDENCIES.md omits Pillow for the layout-§4 logo TGA recipe

findings.title: 11 of 20 source files lack a self-naming first comment
findings.locations: core/Constants.lua:1, core/Database.lua:1, core/Namespace.lua:1, core/PrettyChat.lua:1, core/State.lua:1, core/Util.lua:1, defaults/Defaults.lua:1, defaults/Profile.lua:1, locales/enUS.lua:1, modules/Override.lua:1, settings/Schema.lua:1
findings.evidence: documentation-§9 SHOULD. The *Setup.lua, Panel.lua and Slash.lua files already follow the model.

verification.reason: I counted 20 authored files under core/, defaults/, locales/, modules/ and settings/. The 11 listed ones do not name their own path in the first comment. Database, Util, Profile and enUS start with '-- NS.X — ...', which names the namespace, not the path. Constants, Defaults and Schema have no header comment at all. Where a purpose comment already exists (Database, Util, Profile, enUS, Namespace, PrettyChat, State, Override), rewrite its first line to lead with the path rather than stacking a second header on top.

findings.title: architecture-§1 mandates `local addonName, NS = ...` while lint forbids suppressing 211/addonName (eleven files use `local _, NS = ...`)

verification.reason: The tension is real, but the evidence overstates it. architecture.md:7-11 does say 'Every file MUST start with: local addonName, NS = ...'. lint.md:43, however, forbids only a BLANKET ignore. It explicitly allows 'a narrow per-code ignore in the stanza with a comment saying which files and why'. So both MUSTs can be met literally with per-file 211/addonName stanzas. The .luacheckrc:29-38 comment records a local choice to fix the source rather than suppress, not a lint prohibition. The 11 files that use 'local _, NS = ...' are exactly the ones I counted. Filing this upstream as a wording clarification is still reasonable, and no addon change is needed.
verification.corrected_remediation: Raise upstream as a clarification only. architecture-§1 should read 'destructure both varargs; name the first `_` when the file never reads it', so the collection does not need per-file 211/addonName stanzas that lint.md would allow but that are just noise. findings.title: Reopening a soft-hidden popup in combat with no capture calls protected Hide() on the secure teleport button (ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED)
findings.evidence: PopulateFields' no-capture branch calls fields.teleportBtn:Hide() (SecureActionButtonTemplate child) unguarded; ShowFrame's combat defer (:1014) only covers a popup not shown, so an alpha-0 soft-hidden popup passes through. Reachable via minimap ToggleFrame in combat after Close/gate-hide with no pending capture. Scratch repro recorded mock.blocked = {"<anonymous>:Hide()"}. The already-hidden variant is unverified headlessly (smoke S-001). No test coverage (F-006).
findings.remediation: C-001: route the not-info branch through ConfigureTeleportButton(fields.teleportBtn, fields.teleportIcon, nil), which already defers under lockdown; add a file-scope NO_CAPTURE sentinel so deferTeleportUntilCombatEnds can stash nil and the replay passes nil back. teleportNote:Hide() stays direct. Add red-first test 'frame: reopening a soft-hidden popup in combat with no capture never Hides the secure button'. Move inventory/badge in same commit. Confirm in client via S-001.

verification.reason: modules/Frame.lua:852 PopulateFields' no-info branch calls fields.teleportBtn:Hide() directly. ShowFrame's combat defer (:1014) is `InCombatLockdown() and not (f and f:IsShown())`, and a soft-hidden popup is still IsShown (hidePopup :241-243 only sets alpha 0), so it falls through to preparePopup (:888-893) and then PopulateFields. The path is reachable in play: combat ends test mode or a group-leave wipes the capture, the popup is soft-hidden, and a minimap ToggleFrame (onScreen() is false while soft-hidden) or /wg show runs in combat. endTestMode (:947) already guards this exact call with `not InCombatLockdown()`, which shows the author knew the Hide is protected. Remediation checked: deferTeleportUntilCombatEnds (:526-540) replays only `if pending then`, so a nil stash would be dropped. The NO_CAPTURE sentinel is required, and the finding names it. High is consistent with how the collection grades ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED.

findings.title: preparePopup restores alpha of a soft-hidden popup before the visibility gate; 'Only out of combat' popup reappears mid-fight and cannot be closed by launcher/Escape
findings.locations: modules/Frame.lua:888, modules/Frame.lua:148-151, modules/Frame.lua:1045, modules/Frame.lua:284-286, modules/Frame.lua:1076, settings/Panel.lua:276
findings.evidence: ApplyFrameAlpha does f:SetAlpha(masterAlpha()) with no softHidden knowledge and runs unconditionally in preparePopup; gate asked later. Repro (visibility=outOfCombat): AFTER PULL shown=true alpha=0; AFTER SHOW alpha=1; TOGGLE returned=false alpha=1. /wg show, chat link, minimap, /wg set alpha all reveal it; onScreen() lies so ToggleFrame and ESC fail until combat ends.
findings.remediation: C-002: ApplyFrameAlpha sets f:SetAlpha(softHidden and 0 or masterAlpha()); hoist softHidden/pendingHide local declarations above :148 so they are upvalues. showPopup and hidePopup's real path already clear softHidden first. Add F-006 cases (gate-declined reopen stays alpha 0 and launcher still closes; alpha write while soft-hidden does not reveal). Keep test_frame.lua:877 green. Smoke S-002.

verification.reason: The defect is real. ApplyFrameAlpha (:148-151) does f:SetAlpha(masterAlpha()) with no softHidden check. preparePopup calls it (:888) before the gate is asked (:1045), and the gate-declined branch returns with softHidden still true. The popup is then visible while onScreen() (:285) reports false, so ToggleFrame reopens instead of closing, and the ESC proxy stays hidden. softHidden is declared at :227, below ApplyFrameAlpha, so the hoist in the remediation is needed. Severity lowered to medium. It takes a player action in combat (/wg show, a chat link, the launcher, or an alpha write), it clears itself at PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED through pendingHide, and the title overstates the harm: the popup's own Close button still works, because dismissPopup (:318) goes to hidePopup's soft route and sets alpha 0 again. Only the launcher and Escape fail.
verification.corrected_remediation: As proposed (C-002): ApplyFrameAlpha sets f:SetAlpha(softHidden and 0 or masterAlpha()), with the softHidden/pendingHide declarations hoisted above :148. Also correct the title and the evidence: the footer Close button still dismisses the popup; only the launcher toggle and Escape fail.

findings.title: EventRegistry 'SetItemRef' callback survives the stand-down, gated by IsStoodDown instead of unregistered
findings.evidence: Registered at file load via EventRegistry:RegisterCallback("SetItemRef", ..., WhatGroup); NS.StandDown never calls UnregisterCallback. Comment claims the hooksecurefunc carve-out, but §7 says it MUST NOT be generalized to APIs with a real unregister; EventRegistry has one (modeled in tests/wow_mock.lua:684-687). Anti-pattern #85. Disabled addon still enters Lua on every addon: link click.
findings.remediation: Extract registerLinkCallback() (keep file-load call); NS.StandDown calls EventRegistry:UnregisterCallback("SetItemRef", WhatGroup) when ADDON_LINK_TYPE; NS.StandUp calls registerLinkCallback(). Keep IsStoodDown check for the hooksecurefunc fallback; reword :96-99 comment. Add smoke test (disable, enable, GameMenu Logout, click details link) to docs/smoke-tests.md. If in-client taint appears, revert and file a slash-commands-§7 Documented deviations row instead.

verification.reason: The defect is real. core/WhatGroup.lua:108-111 registers the EventRegistry 'SetItemRef' callback at file load, and NS.StandDown (:329-349) never unregisters it. The gate relies on IsStoodDown (:100), and the comment at :96-99 applies the hooksecurefunc carve-out to it. slash-commands.md:189 says an addon MUST NOT generalize that carve-out to anything with a real unregister, and EventRegistry has one (the wow_mock models it at :684). Severity lowered to low: the reachable impact is one cheap Lua call on each addon-link click while disabled, and nothing is shown or written. The rule is a MUST, but the harm is negligible.

findings.title: global.schemaVersion default equals current version, so AceDB strips it at logout and the first real migration is skipped for every existing user
findings.evidence: global = { schemaVersion = NS.SCHEMA_VERSION or 1 }; AceDB removeDefaults (AceDB-3.0.lua:134, :425) strips values equal to default, so no SV file carries a stamp; when SCHEMA_VERSION becomes 2 the default reads 2 and 1->2 never runs. `or NS.SCHEMA_VERSION` at Database.lua:27 is dead. Existing test sets schemaVersion=0 explicitly and cannot see this (testing-§12 near-miss). The savedvariables-§1 template prescribes the same shape (collection-wide).
findings.remediation: Local C-003: declare global.schemaVersion = 0 (pre-versioning) default, keep NS.SCHEMA_VERSION = 1; RunMigrations steps 0->1 (no-op) and stores 1 which persists; delete dead `or`; document steps must be idempotent against a fresh default profile. Rewrite 'BuildDefaults seeds global.schemaVersion' test to pin 0; add red-under case: boot, run removeDefaults strip, re-boot with SCHEMA_VERSION=2 and a 1->2 step, assert step ran. Upstream U-1: amend WowAddonStandards savedvariables-§1 template to declare 0 and explain the AceDB strip; standard minor bump. Local fix does not wait for U-1. Smoke S-003.

verification.reason: settings/Schema.lua:609 sets the global.schemaVersion default to NS.SCHEMA_VERSION (1). AceDB removeDefaults (libs/AceDB-3.0/AceDB-3.0.lua:134, called at :425 on logout) strips values equal to their default, so the stamp never persists. Once SCHEMA_VERSION becomes 2, the default reads 2, `from` equals 2, and the 1->2 step is skipped. `or NS.SCHEMA_VERSION` at core/Database.lua:27 is dead under AceDB defaults. standards/savedvariables.md:10 and :23 prescribe the same shape, so upstream routing to WowAddonStandards is correct, and the local fix does not need to wait for it. The defect is latent because no migration exists yet, but it would silently lose the first one for every existing user. Medium is justified.

findings.title: 16 NS.Debug call sites build the message (concatenation/tostring) before the call

" status=" .. tostring(newStatus)) allocates on every LFG_LIST_APPLICATION_STATUS_UPDATED with debug off; values bypass the sink's safeToString. verification.reason: The defect is real. A grep over core/modules/settings finds 39 NS.Debug calls, and the cited sites build the message with `..`/tostring before the call (for example core/WhatGroup.lua:973, :916-918; modules/Frame.lua:504-507, :890-892; settings/Schema.lua:398, :465). debug-logging.md:56 says MUST NOT, and the ARCHITECTURE events-frames-taint-§8 row covers only §8. findings.title: Terminal LFG application statuses (timedout, invitedeclined, failed) missing from APPLICATION_ENDED
findings.evidence: Ends only on declined, declined_full, declined_delisted, cancelled; timed-out/declined-invite captures linger in capturesByResult/pendingApplications until next inviteaccepted or group-leave wipe. Bounded, id-keyed, no cross-invite effect. Status spellings unverified for 12.1.0.
findings.remediation: C-010: first record exact status strings in client (/etrace LFG_LIST_APPLICATION_STATUS_UPDATED, smoke S-008), then add them to APPLICATION_ENDED and one tests/test_capture.lua case per status pinning the capture drop; move inventory/badge.

verification.reason: core/WhatGroup.lua:936-941: APPLICATION_ENDED holds only declined, declined_full, declined_delisted and cancelled. Blizzard's LFG application statuses also include timedout, invitedeclined and failed. Those leave the capture in capturesByResult/pendingApplications until the group-leave wipe (:882/:1029). The leak is bounded and keyed by id, so low is right. Capturing the exact status strings in-client before coding, as the remediation says, is appropriate.

findings.title: Two settings-category fields written and never read, pinned by a test
findings.evidence: WhatGroup._settingsCategory and _parentSettingsCategory have no production reader (OpenOptionsPanel holds its own); test asserts non-nil, pinning dead state. grep -rn _settingsCategory libs/ is empty.
findings.remediation: C-011: delete the two assignments and comment; drop the two asserts in tests/test_panel.lua:90-91 (inside a larger case, count unchanged); re-run --list.

verification.reason: The defect is real. settings/Panel.lua:387 and :390 write _settingsCategory and _parentSettingsCategory, and no runtime code reads them (libs/ has no hits either). tests/test_panel.lua:90-91 only asserts that they are non-nil. The remediation misses the docs that describe these fields. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:323 and docs/settings-panel.md:260 both say Panel.lua 'records' the two handles. docs/midnight-quirks.md:38-40 uses self._settingsCategory in its example. Deleting the fields without updating those pages would leave the docs describing code that no longer exists (documentation drift).
verification.corrected_remediation: C-011: delete the two assignments and their comment at settings/Panel.lua:387-390. Drop the two asserts at tests/test_panel.lua:90-91 and keep the rest of the case (the test count is unchanged), then re-run --list. In the same commit, remove the sentence about the recorded handles in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:323 and docs/settings-panel.md:260. Rewrite the docs/midnight-quirks.md:38-40 example with a local category variable so it does not reference self._settingsCategory.

findings.title: Minimap row's CLI path global.minimap.hide reads inverted (true while visible)
findings.evidence: /wg get global.minimap.hide answers true while the button is shown; /wg set ... false hides it. Path and inversion mandated by launcher-§3 and options-ui-§15, so WhatGroup is compliant; collection-wide wart.
findings.remediation: Upstream U-2: WowAddonStandards rules on a shown-polarity CLI alias for the minimap row while storage stays minimap.hide; if adopted, LibKa0s OptionsCompose/Slash gains an alias field (minor bump) and each addon re-vendors the whole libs/LibKa0s folder in its own commit. No local edit (renaming the path is rejected by launcher-§3).

verification.reason: settings/Schema.lua:361 `local MINIMAP_PATH = "global.minimap.hide"`, with the inversion documented at :355-360. launcher.md:42 requires storing at `minimap.hide` and forbids a parallel show key (anti-pattern #81). options-ui.md:365 defers storage and inversion to launcher-§3. So WhatGroup is compliant, and the only fix is an upstream CLI alias ruling followed by a LibKa0s change and a re-vendor. Routing is correct. A local rename would break launcher-§3.

findings.title: Teleport configure allocates three fresh script closures per call
findings.locations: modules/Frame.lua:403-456, modules/Frame.lua:411, modules/Frame.lua:416, modules/Frame.lua:423, modules/Frame.lua:444-449, modules/Frame.lua:516-523
findings.evidence: applyTeleportAction builds OnEnter/OnLeave/PreClick closures every configure; with resolveTeleportState's per-call table this is most of showFrameRepeat's 1872.5 B/iter. Once per popup show; hygiene.
findings.remediation: C-006: define onTeleportEnter/onTeleportLeave/onTeleportPreClick once at file scope reading btn.__wgSpellID/__wgSpellName from self; re-run tests/perf.lua, record new showFrameRepeat in docs/performance.md and lower the scenario ceiling (measured + 24) in the same change. Smoke S-006.

verification.reason: modules/Frame.lua:403-456 applyTeleportAction creates fresh closures on every configure: OnEnter (:411), OnLeave (:416), PreClick (:423), plus a duplicate OnEnter/OnLeave pair on the known-but-not-ready branch (:444-449). resolveTeleportState (:516-523) returns a new table on every call. This runs once per popup show, so Low hygiene is justified. The file-scope handler remediation is sound as long as spellID and spellName are stored on the button before the handlers are set.

findings.title: Landing-page logo path hand-types the folder name

findings.title: documentation-§3 Tier 1 settings-panel.md row says 'Tab | Covers (one row per settings subcategory)', contradicting its own granularity

findings.title: Three upstream standard text issues: AUDIT.md re-vendor check grade contradicts step 5; toc-file-§3 says 'currently 120007'; layout-§4 '.png ships' ambiguity
findings.locations: WowAddonStandards AUDIT.md step 4; standards toc-file-§3; standards layout-§4; .pkgmeta:27-31
findings.evidence: (1) AUDIT.md calls a missing re-vendor bundle 'a High finding' while step 5 grades doc-only failures Low (see WG-71). (2) toc-file-§3 literal 120007 vs collection 120100. (3) layout-§4 says editable .png 'ships but is never loaded' while .pkgmeta deliberately excludes it.
findings.remediation: WowAddonStandards: (1) change to 'is a finding (grade by impact, step 5)'; (2) update to 120100 or drop the literal and point at ADDONS.md; (3) state whether 'ships' is normative; if so WhatGroup .pkgmeta:30-31 needs a row or change. Re-check after amendment (S6-2).

verification.reason: (1) AUDIT.md:341-342, in step 4, says 'A tag vendored with no bundle naming it and no Documented deviations row ... is a **High** finding'. Step 5's impact grading (AUDIT.md:861-865) reserves High for user/SV/session impact, so this is a real contradiction. (2) toc-file.md:10 and :61 say 'currently `120007`'. (3) layout.md:125 says the editable .png 'ships but is never loaded', but WhatGroup .pkgmeta (the media/logos/*.png and *.jpg ignore lines, ~:30-31) deliberately excludes it from the package. All three are standards-text issues and belong upstream.
